revision.text:
{{External|rs|rsc}} {{Infobox Location |name = Seers' Village |image = [[File:Seers Village.png|300px]] |release = [[25 March]] [[2002]] |update = Latest RuneScape News (25 March 2002) |aka = Seers' |members = Yes |location = [[Kandarin]] |race = [[Human]]s, predominantly [[Seer]]s |teleport = [[Camelot Teleport]] |music = [[Overture]] |map = {{Map|name=Seers' Village|x=2710|y=3485|height=250|zoom=1}} |type = settlement |leagueRegion = Kandarin }} {{Relativelocation |location = Seers' Village |north = Sinclair Mansion |west = Hemenster |south = Keep Le Faye |east = Catherby }} '''Seers' Village''' is a small settlement to the west of [[Camelot]]. The mighty city of [[Ardougne]] is to the south, and [[Rellekka]] and [[Sinclair Mansion]] are to the north. ==Transportation== {| class="wikitable" !Name !Teleport destination !Requirements !Walk |- |{{Plink|Camelot Teleport}} |[[Camelot]] |{{SCP|Magic|45}} or [[Camelot teleport (tablet)|Tablet]] |Very short |- |{{Plink|Catherby Teleport}} |[[Catherby]] |{{SCP|Magic|87}} or [[Catherby teleport (tablet)|Tablet]] |Short |- |{{Plink|Kandarin headgear 3}} |[[Sherlock]] |Completion of the hard [[Kandarin Diary]] |Short |- |{{Plink|Fairy ring|pic=Fairy ring (Construction) icon}} {{Fairycode|als}} |[[McGrubor's Wood]] |Partial completion of [[Fairytale II]] |Short |- |{{Plink|Combat bracelet}} |[[Ranging Guild]] |Must be charged |Short |- |}
==Notable features== ===Camelot=== {{main|Camelot}} Located just north-east of the village, [[Camelot]] provides the closest [[teleport]] location.
===Bank=== Before the release of the [[Grand Exchange]], the [[Seers' Village bank]] used to be a very popular trading spot. From here, most [[Fletching]] items such as [[flax]] and [[bow string]]s were sold. The bank was also a popular trading arena for [[Treasure Trail]] rewards and rare items.
===Trees=== Seers' Village is a very popular [[Woodcutting]] destination. In total, the village and close surrounding area contain six [[yew tree]]s, six [[maple tree]]s, ten [[willow tree]]s, and multiple [[oak tree]]s.
===Elemental Workshop=== {{main|Elemental Workshop (dungeon)|Elemental Workshop|Elemental Workshop II}} The [[Elemental Workshop (dungeon)|Elemental Workshop]] is accessible through the building with the [[anvil]] in it and is used in [[Elemental Workshop]] and [[Elemental Workshop II]]. The book containing the key to access the workshop (and consequently start the quest) is found in a bookshelf inside a house directly south of the workshop.
===Agility course=== {{main|Seers' Village Rooftop Course}} Players with 60 [[Agility]] can use the [[Seers' Village Rooftop Course|rooftop course]], by climbing up the wall on the south-eastern side of the bank. The course finishes in front of the church.
===Church=== {{Main|Seers' Village church}} [[File:Seers' Village chapel.png|thumb|The chapel and its graveyard.]] The church in the village has 3 [[yew tree]]s in its courtyard, as well as an entrance to [[Death's Domain]]. The church is at the end of the rooftop agility course. Within it is an [[altar]] to restore [[Prayer]] at and a [[church organ]].
===Flax field=== {{main|Flax field}} If players have completed the [[Kandarin Diary]], the [[flax keeper]] will exchange players a certain amount of flax for bow strings each day, increasing as the players completes more of the diary.
===Beehive field=== The beehive field is located south-east of Seers' Village. It's just to the east of the flax field. As suggested by the name, it contains many beehives. These beehives are used during the [[Merlin's Crystal]] quest by using [[insect repellant]] found in [[Catherby]] on a hive. Players may also be teleported here to help re-construct a hive in a [[random event]].
===Saradomin altar=== The [[Saradomin]] altar is located north-west of the flax field. Inside the Graveyard located at the front of this altar are several [[yew tree]]s for [[Woodcutting]].
===Poison Salesman=== The [[Poison Salesman]] loiters west of the bank in the bar and plays a role in [[The Fremennik Trials]] and [[Murder Mystery]] quests.
===Forester's Arms Pub=== {{main|Forester's Arms}} The local pub is one of the target bars in [[Alfred Grimhand's Barcrawl]]. It is also a common place for players training their [[Ranged]] skill due to the fact that there are many level 2 [[men]] and [[women]] in the pub with many tables to prevent retaliation.
===Coal Trucks depot=== North of the bar is a small building with several [[Coal Trucks]] inside it. From here, players can retrieve all of the [[coal]] mined from the coal trucks, providing it was loaded into the carts at the coal trucks. A coal cart can hold up to 120 coal, but it can hold more coal after completion of certain difficulties of the [[Kandarin Diary]].
===McGrubor's Wood=== {{main|McGrubor's Wood}} To the west of Seers' Village, [[McGrubor's Wood]] is used in the [[Fishing Contest]] and [[Plague City]] quests. The residents will not let players through the front entrance, so players will need to squeeze through some railings at the back. Be careful as level 44 [[guard dog]]s patrol the area.
===Courthouse=== {{main|Seers' Village courthouse}} Located south-east of the bank, the courthouse is instrumental in the [[King's Ransom]] quest. Here, you defend [[Anna Sinclair]], and strive to achieve a non-guilty verdict. The courthouse replaced the [[Party Room]] with an update to Seers' Village.
==Related quests== *[[Elemental Workshop]] *[[Elemental Workshop II]] *[[Holy Grail]] *[[King's Ransom]] *[[Merlin's Crystal]] *[[Murder Mystery]] *[[One Small Favour]]
==Monsters== *[[Highwayman]] (level 5) *[[Guard dog]] (level 44) *[[Wolf]] (level 64) - These wolves are to the north and past the [[Sinclair Mansion]].
==Changes== {{Subject changes header}} {{Subject changes |date = 10 December 2014 |update = The Trading Post |change = The poll booth in Seers' Village bank has been returned. }} {{Subject changes |date = 9 January 2014 |update = Minigame Grouping |change = A small hill forming at Seers Village has been flattened. }} {{Subject changes footer}} ==Trivia== *The bank contains a secret message in Morse Code. If an open bank booth is interpreted as a dot ( • ) and a closed bank booth is interpreted as a dash ( – ), the bank booths spell out the word "items" ( •• – • –– ••• ). {{Seers' Village}} [[Category:Kandarin]]

revision.text:
{{External|rs}} {{Infobox Location |name = Seers' Village courthouse |image = [[File:Seers' Village courthouse.png]] |release = [[24 July]] [[2007]] |update = King's Ransom |members = Yes |location = [[Seers' Village]] |music = [[Lore and Order]] |map = {{Map|name=Seers' Village courthouse|x=2735|y=3469|height=250|zoom=2}} |type = building |leagueRegion = Kandarin }} The '''Seers' Village courthouse''' is a building located south-east of the [[Seers' Village]] [[bank]]. The courthouse plays a major role in the [[King's Ransom]] quest. In the quest, the player must defend [[Anna]] from the [[Prosecutor]] and rebut several pieces of evidence that indicate Anna being the murderer of [[Lord Sinclair]], in order to convince the [[Judge]] and Jury of her innocence.
Originally, the [[Party Room]] was located where the courthouse currently is. With the release of King's Ransom, the Party Room was moved to [[Falador]] and the Courtroom replaced it in [[Seers' Village]]. Reference is made to this during the quest, when [[party balloon]]s fall from the ceiling.
==Trivia== *[[Lore and Order]], the music track that plays in the building, is a play on the words ''law and order'', often referred to in a legal or political context.
{{King's Ransom}} [[Category:Kandarin]] [[Category:Municipal buildings]]

{{External|rs}} {{Infobox Location |name = Senntisten |image = [[File:The Dig Site - Senntisten.png|300px]] |release = [[9 July]] [[2003]] |update = New Digsite Quest! |aka = The Digsite |members = Yes |location = [[Misthalin]] |teleport = {{*}} [[Digsite pendant]]
{{*}} [[Ancient Magicks]]
([[Senntisten Teleport]]) |music = [[Venture]], [[Venture 2]] |map = {{Map|name=Senntisten|x=3354|y=3390|height=250|zoom=1}} |leagueRegion = Misthalin }} {{Relativelocation |location = Senntisten
(Digsite) |north = Wilderness |west = Varrock |south = Exam Centre |east = Morytania }} '''Senntisten''' was the capital city of the [[Zarosian Empire]], which existed during the [[Second Age|Second]] and [[Third Age]]. According to archaeologists, it was home to a massive temple complex, and occupied roughly the area east of modern-day [[Varrock]] and parts of [[Silvarea]], making it one of the largest known cities in [[Gielinor]]'s history. The city continued to act as the capital after the fall of [[Zaros]] at the hands of his general [[Zamorak]], surviving throughout most of the [[God Wars]] until it was eventually conquered by [[Zamorak]]ian forces. Under Zamorakian occupation, the city was destroyed, and was later conquered by [[Saradomin]]ists. They built the city [[Saranthium]] where the Zarosian capital once stood. ==Present day== Senntisten lies at the Varrockian [[Digsite]] and is currently being excavated by the [[Varrock Museum]]. During [[The Dig Site]] quest, the player finds a [[Ancient talisman|Zarosian symbol]] and an ancient [[Stone tablet (The Dig Site)|tablet]] in an undiscovered temple ruin. Those with the knowledge of [[Ancient Magicks]] can utilise a Zarosian [[spell]], [[Senntisten Teleport]], to teleport here. This spell requires 60 [[Magic]], two [[law runes]], and one [[soul rune]]. The [[Digsite pendant]] can also be used. ==Trivia== *The city's name appears to be derived from the Hungarian phrase ''Szent Isten'', meaning "holy god". {{Zarosian Empire}} {{The Dig Site}} {{Digsite}} [[Category:Lore]] [[Category:Locations that do not appear in-game]] {{Places of worship}}

revision.text:
{{External|rs=Senntisten teleport (item)}} {{otheruses|the teleport tablet|the teleport spell|Senntisten Teleport}} {{Infobox Item |name = Senntisten teleport |image = [[File:Senntisten teleport (tablet).png]] |release = [[18 September]] [[2014]] |update = Bounty Hunter |members = Yes |quest = No |tradeable = Yes |equipable = No |stackable = Yes |noteable = No |options = Break, Drop |examine = A teleport to Senntisten. |value = 1 |weight = 0.000 |exchange = Yes |gemwname = Senntisten teleport (tablet) |id = 12782 }} [[File:Senntisten teleport (tablet) detail.png|left|130px]] The '''Senntisten teleport''' is a [[magic tablet]] that can be broken by players to [[Teleportation|teleport]] to the [[Digsite]] [[Exam Centre]], providing that they have completed [[Desert Treasure I]]. Players can create this item on the [[Lectern (Ancient)|ancient lectern]] by the altar inside the [[Ancient Pyramid]] with a piece of [[soft clay]], 2 [[law rune]]s, and 1 [[soul rune]], as well as level 60 [[Magic]] while being on the [[Ancient Magicks]] spellbook. [[File:Teleport Tablet.gif|left|thumb|130px|A player breaking a teleport tablet]] The player '''does not''' need to have the relevant Magic level to use the tablet, which shares the same rule with all tablets and the player will not receive any [[experience]], although making the teleport tablet does give 70 experience in Magic. ==Destination== {{Map|3320,3337|mtype=square|r=2|align=left}}{{clear|left}} ==Creation== {{Recipe |skill1 = Magic |skill1lvl = 60 |skill1boostable = Yes |skill1exp = 70 |notes = {{plink|Ancient Magicks|pic=Ancient spellbook}} active |members = Yes |ticks = 2 |ticksnote = Auto-creating is 2, then 4 ticks. |facilities = Lectern (Ancient) |mat1 = Law rune |mat2 = Soul rune |mat4 = Soft clay |mat1quantity = 2 |output1 = Senntisten teleport (tablet) |output1txt = Senntisten teleport }} ==Item sources== {{Drop sources|Senntisten teleport (tablet)}} ===Shop locations=== {{Store locations list|Senntisten teleport (tablet)}} ==Changes== {{Subject changes header}} {{Subject changes |date = 30 September 2020 |update = Last Poll 72 Updates |poll = Old School Content Poll 72: Costume Rooms & Skilling |change = Players can now create magic tablets of Ancient Magicks teleport spells at the lectern inside the [[Ancient Pyramid]]. }} {{Subject changes |date = 23 April 2020 |update = Bounty Hunter Returns |poll = |change = Senntisten teleports now cost 10,000 points each. }} {{Subject changes |date = 28 November 2019 |update = Ashihama Rewards Beta and Sire Changes |poll = |change = Six Senntisten teleports are now given per point instead of four. }} {{Subject changes |date = 12 October 2017 |update = Dragon Slayer II reqs, QoL and a look at the coming weeks! |poll = |change = The examine text was changed. Previously, it was "''A tablet containing a magic spell.''" }} {{Subject changes |date = 12 May 2016 |update = Necromancy Teleport Tablets |poll = Old School Content Poll 41: Bank placeholders & Skillcapes |change = The teleport tablet was given another graphical update. }} {{Subject changes |date = 30 April 2015 |update = Mutagens, Mo & Much More |poll = |change = The teleport tablet was given a [[graphical updates|graphical update]]. }} {{Subject changes footer}} ===Gallery (historical)=== {|style="text-align: center" cellpadding="15" |[[File:Senntisten teleport (tablet) (v1) detail.png|center|300x150px]] |[[File:Senntisten teleport (tablet) (v2) detail.png|center|300x150px]] |[[File:Senntisten teleport (tablet) detail.png|center|300x150px]] |- |[[File:Senntisten teleport (tablet) v1.png|center]] |[[File:Senntisten teleport (tablet) v2.png|center]] |[[File:Senntisten teleport (tablet).png|center]] |- |18 September 2014 –

{{otheruses|the book|the former human named Serafina|The Maiden of Sugadinti|the character's diary|Serafina's diary}} {{Infobox Item |name = Serafina |image = [[File:Serafina (book).png]] |release = [[4 January]] [[2018]] |update = Dragon Slayer II |aka = The Tale of Serafina |members = Yes |quest = No |tradeable = No |equipable = No |stackable = No |noteable = No |options = Read, Drop |examine = The Tale of Serafina by James Locke. |value = 1 |weight = 0.510 |id = 22047 }} [[File:Serafina (book) detail.png|left|150px]] '''Serafina''', or '''The Tale of Serafina''' is a book written by James Locke that can be found in the library of the [[Myths' Guild]] after completing [[Dragon Slayer II]].
The book speaks of the Tale of [[The Maiden of Sugadinti|Serafina]], in which she takes on the [[Theatre of Blood]] and survived all of the challenges within, and was granted freedom from the [[blood tithe]]s as her reward. However, it is discovered during the [[quest]] [[A Taste of Hope]] and in [[Serafina's diary|her diary]] that the tale was simply a ruse to instill false hope into the citizens of [[Meiyerditch]] so that they could provide entertainment for the vampyres.
If lost, it can be reclaimed from the Myths' Guild library, or from a [[bookcase]] within a [[player-owned house]].

{{External|rs}} {{Infobox NPC |name = Sergeant Mossfists |image = [[File:Sergeant Mossfists.png|270px]] |release = [[24 April]] [[2007]] |update = Another Slice of H.A.M. |level = 51 |members = Yes |race = [[goblin (race)|Goblin]] |quest = [[Another Slice of H.A.M.]] |location = [[Lumbridge Swamp]] |gender = Male |options = Talk-to |examine = An ugly green creature... but don't say that to his face! |map = {{Map|name=Sergeant Mossfists|x=3170|y=3172|r=6|mtype=square}} |id = 5161 |leagueRegion = Misthalin }} [[File:Sergeant Mossfists chathead.png|left]] '''Sergeant Mossfists''' is a [[goblin (race)|goblin]] sergeant from [[Goblin Village]], and the strongest and most powerful warrior loyal to [[General Bentnoze]] there, having a combat level of 51 (though he is unattackable). He and his rival, [[Sergeant Slimetoes]], can be found and interacted with only during [[Another Slice of H.A.M.]].
During the [[quest]], they help the player get to the [[Humans Against Monsters|H.A.M.]] tunnel to free [[Zanik]], who has been captured by the H.A.M. agent [[Sigmund]]. Mossfists, along with Slimetoes, help the player by distracting the guards and allowing them to sneak past.
==Dialogue== {{Hastranscript|npc}}
{{Another Slice of H.A.M.}} [[Category:Goblins]] [[Category:Bandosians]]

{{External|rs}} {{Infobox NPC |name = Sergeant Slimetoes |image = [[File:Sergeant Slimetoes.png|270px]] |release = [[24 April]] [[2007]] |update = Another Slice of H.A.M. |level = 51 |members = Yes |race = [[goblin (race)|Goblin]] |quest = [[Another Slice of H.A.M.]] |location = [[Lumbridge Swamp]] |gender = Male |options = Talk-to |examine = An ugly green creature... but don't say that to his face! |map = {{Map|name=Sergeant Slimetoes|x=3170|y=3172|r=6|mtype=square}} |id = 5162 |leagueRegion = Misthalin }} [[File:Sergeant Slimetoes chathead.png|left]] '''Sergeant Slimetoes''' is a [[goblin (race)|goblin]] sergeant from [[Goblin Village]], and the most powerful and able warrior under [[General Wartface]]'s banner, having a combat level of 51, which is high for a goblin. He and his rival [[Sergeant Mossfists]] can only be found or interacted with during [[Another Slice of H.A.M.]].
During the [[quest]], they help the player to get to [[Humans Against Monsters|H.A.M.]] tunnel to rescue [[Zanik]] from [[Sigmund]]'s plot to send the [[Dorgeshuun]] and the [[dwarves]] to war with each other. Slimetoes and Mossfists play a small but important part in the quest by attacking one of the [[H.A.M. Guard]]s in the cellar while the player sneaks past.

{{Another Slice of H.A.M.}} [[Category:Goblins]] [[Category:Bandosians]]

{{External|rs}} {{Infobox Item |defver = 4 |version1 = 1 dose |version2 = 2 dose |version3 = 3 dose |version4 = 4 dose |bucketname1 = (1) |bucketname2 = (2) |bucketname3 = (3) |bucketname4 = (4) |name1 = Serum 208 (1) |name2 = Serum 208 (2) |name3 = Serum 208 (3) |name4 = Serum 208 (4) |image1 = [[File:Serum 208 (1).png]] |image2 = [[File:Serum 208 (2).png]] |image3 = [[File:Serum 208 (3).png]] |image4 = [[File:Serum 208 (4).png]] |release = [[18 October]] [[2004]] |update = Mortton Shades and Mage Armour |members = Yes |quest = [[Shades of Mort'ton]] |tradeable = No |equipable = No |stackable = No |noteable = No |options = Empty, Drop |examine1 = 1 dose permanent serum 208 as described in Herbi Flax's diary. |examine2 = 2 doses permanent serum 208 as described in Herbi Flax's diary. |examine3 = 3 doses permanent serum 208 as described in Herbi Flax's diary. |examine4 = 4 doses permanent serum 208 as described in Herbi Flax's diary. |value1 = 11 |value2 = 13 |value3 = 13 |value4 = 14 |weight1 = 0.020 |weight2 = 0.025 |weight3 = 0.030 |weight4 = 0.035 |id1 = 3419 |id2 = 3418 |id3 = 3417 |id4 = 3416 }} {{Synced switch |version1 = [[File:Serum 208 (1) detail.png|left|120px]] |version2 = [[File:Serum 208 (2) detail.png|left|120px]] |version3 = [[File:Serum 208 (3) detail.png|left|120px]] |version4 = [[File:Serum 208 (4) detail.png|left|120px|class=pageimage]] }} '''Serum 208''' is a permanent cure for the [[afflicted]] villagers of [[Mort'ton]]. It is used during or after the [[Shades of Mort'ton]] quest to turn Afflicted NPCs back into normal characters so the player can interact with them on a permanent basis. Whether it is during or after the quest, it can be created by using [[Serum 207]] on the sacred flame at the rebuilt temple. Players must have at least 20% sanctity in order to convert Serum 207 into Serum 208, consuming 5% sanctity per dose. Therefore, it is recommended to convert Serum 207 with at least 2 doses to permanently cure the necessary NPCs (total of two) without wasting additional sanctity. Unlike Serum 207, it cannot be stored in [[Potion storage]]. It is suggested it be used on [[Razmire Keelgan]], so he will always be coherent for the player and open his general and builder's stores. When used on an afflicted villager, they will turn into [[Mort'ton locals]] and reward the player with items such as [[Olive oil]], [[Tarromin]], and [[Coins]]. Although it is a "permanent" cure, ordinary villagers will always return to their afflicted state. ([[Razmire Keelgan|Razmire]] and [[Ulsquire Shauncy]] are the exceptions - although they may appear to turn back to their afflicted state after some time, they will become cured when talked to.) Therefore, there is no way to permanently "clean up" Mort'ton. On average, curing Mort'ton villagers returns more Tarromin than what is spent for Serum 208 potions, making this a slow, but steady way of obtaining Tarromin. ==Creation== {{Switch infobox |text1 = 1 dose |item1 = {{Recipe |skill1 = Herblore |skill1lvl = 15 |skill1boostable = Yes |skill1exp = 0 |notes = {{SCP|Quest}} [[Shades of Mort'ton]]

{{SCP|Minigame}} 20% sanctity in the [[Shades of Mort'ton (minigame)|Shades of Mort'ton minigame]] |members = Yes |ticks = |facilities = Fire altar (Flamtaer) |mat1 = Serum 207 (2) |mat1quantity = 1 |output1 = Serum 208 (2) |output1quantity = 1 |output1cost = No }} |text3 = 3 dose |item3 = {{Recipe |skill1 = Herblore |skill1lvl = 15 |skill1boostable = Yes |skill1exp = 0 |notes = {{SCP|Quest}} [[Shades of Mort'ton]]
{{SCP|Minigame}} 20% sanctity in the [[Shades of Mort'ton (minigame)|Shades of Mort'ton minigame]] |members = Yes |ticks = |facilities = Fire altar (Flamtaer) |mat1 = Serum 207 (3) |mat1quantity = 1 |output1 = Serum 208 (3) |output1quantity = 1 |output1cost = No }} |text4 = 4 dose |item4 = {{Recipe |skill1 = Herblore |skill1lvl = 15 |skill1boostable = Yes |skill1exp = 0 |notes = {{SCP|Quest}} [[Shades of Mort'ton]]

{{External|rs}} {{otheruses|the NPCs in player-owned houses}} {{Map|2668,3332|mtype=square|r=6|align=right|caption=Location of the servants.}} A '''Servant''' is an [[Non-player character|NPC]] that players can hire for various services in their [[player-owned house]]. There are five different servants, each having a higher [[Construction]] level requirement and offering better services than the last. ==Hiring a servant== {{Hiring servants}} ==Types of servants== {| class="wikitable align-center-1 align-center-3 align-center-6" ! colspan="2" | Servant !{{SCP|Construction}}
Level !Cost !Food served !Sawmill !Capacity !Cost per trip !Minimum cost per item !Trip time !Maximum cost per hour |- |[[File:Rick chathead.png|x50px]] |[[Rick]] |20 |500 coins |[[Shrimps]] |No |6 items |{{Coins|{{#expr:500/8 round 0}}}} |{{Coins|{{#expr:500/8/6 round 0}}}} |60s |{{Coins|{{#expr:500/8/60*3600 round 0}}}} |- |[[File:Maid chathead.png|x50px]] |[[Maid]] |25 |1,000 coins |[[Stew]] |No |10 items |{{Coins|{{#expr:1000/8 round 0}}}} |{{Coins|{{#expr:1000/8/10 round 0}}}} |30s |{{Coins|{{#expr:1000/8/30*3600 round 0}}}} |- |[[File:Cook (servant) chathead.png|x50px]] |[[Cook (servant)|Cook]] |30 |3,000 coins |[[Pineapple pizza]] |Yes |16 items |{{Coins|{{#expr:3000/8 round 0}}}} |{{Coins|{{#expr:3000/8/16 round 0}}}} |17s |{{Coins|{{#expr:3000/8/17*3600 round 0}}}} |- |[[File:Butler chathead.png|x50px]] |[[Butler]] |40 |5,000 coins |[[Chocolate cake]] |Yes |20 items |{{Coins|{{#expr:5000/8 round 0}}}} |{{Coins|{{#expr:5000/8/20 round 0}}}} |12s |{{Coins|{{#expr:5000/8/12*3600 round 0}}}} |- |[[File:Demon butler chathead.png|x50px]] |[[Demon butler]] |50 |10,000 coins |[[Curry]] |Yes |26 items |{{Coins|{{#expr:10000/8 round 0}}}} |{{Coins|{{#expr:10000/8/26 round 0}}}} |7s |{{Coins|{{#expr:10000/8/7*3600 round 0}}}} |} ==Services== {{Servant services}} ==Payment== Servants only accept money directly from the player's inventory or by storing coins in a [[servant's money bag]]. After using a servant's paid services eight times, players are required to either pay or fire them. The servant cannot be used for anything else before the payment is made; the servant will temporarily keep the items and will not give them until the player pays. Any items that the servant is holding will be deposited in the bank if the player leaves the house or if the servant is fired. ==Changes== {{Subject changes header}} {{Subject changes |date = 14 January 2026 |update = New Player Improvements Round 2 |change = Servants now correctly repeat their last sawmill task when making [[Ironwood plank|ironwood]], [[Camphor plank|camphor]], and [[rosewood plank]]s. }} {{Subject changes |date = 30 July 2015 |update = Custom F-Keys & Music Cape |change = It is now possible to call your PoH Servant using the house options menu found in settings. }} {{Subject changes |date = 30 April 2015 |update = Mutagens, Mo & Much More |change = Added missing full stops on some POH Servant dialogue. }} {{Subject changes |date = 8 May 2014 |update = Your banks, it has tabs! |change = POH Butlers now spawn more reliably when fetching items. }} {{Subject changes |date = 6 February 2007 |update = Fremennik Isles |change = Servants will now require players to enter their [[Bank PIN]] when they ask them to withdraw items from their [[bank]]. }} {{Subject changes footer}} ==References== {{Reflist}} {{Servants}} [[Category:Bank PIN protection]]

revision.text:
{{External|wp=Crash (computing)}} [[File:Server blackout 2007.png|thumb|The old secondary world-select menu during the third server blackout, circa 2007.]] A '''server blackout''' is the unexpected crash of a [[server]], typically resulting in all players being [[logged out]] for an extended period of time. Blackouts usually affect most, if not all, game servers and may affect other ''RuneScape'' facilities, such as the main website.
Blackouts are generally caused by a technical failure on the part of [[Jagex]]. Players who suffer from blackouts can only wait until the problem is fixed by Jagex. In some cases, a [[rollback]] is necessary. A rollback is an operation that returns server databases to their previous state from before the blackout occurred. On rare occasions where a rollback is performed, any changes that occurred between the crash and the previous state are lost. This includes gained [[experience]], [[trade]] transactions, [[quest]] progress, etc. Rollbacks typically revert the servers to the state they were in anywhere from 15 minutes to one hour prior.
Under rare and severe circumstances, Jagex might intentionally implement server blackout. A renowned example of server blackout was the infamous [[rsw:Falador Massacre|Falador Massacre]], utilised to cease [[bug abuse]] and take action towards the massacre leaders without a rollback.
During an intentional server blackout, worlds on the select screen are listed as "OFFLINE", as opposed to displaying the number of players logged in. However, on an unexpected crash, the login server simply assumes that nobody is connected to that server.
On November 22, 2022, the longest unintentional server blackout occurred due to power failure at one of Jagex’s external data centres. Jagex was able to recover by November 23 around 3:00 GMT. There was no [[Rollback|server rollback]]. Jagex did mention offering "Make Good" options to compensate players for the blackout, however the status of these options is still unknown.
[[Category:Mechanics]]

{{Infobox Item |name = Serving platter |image = [[File:Serving platter.png]] |release = [[10 December]] [[2025]] |update = Christmas Event 2025 |members = No |quest = No |tradeable = No |bankable = No |equipable = No |stackable = No |noteable = No |options = Inspect, Destroy |destroy = You can get another from the Cook at the Blue Moon Inn. |examine = I can carry food and drinks on this. |value = 50 |alchable = No |weight = 0.050 |id = 32926 }} [[File:Serving platter detail.png|130px|left]]'''Serving platter''' is an item used in the [[2025 Christmas event]]. During the event, the player can place drinks on the platter, including [[beer]], [[dwarven stout]], [[cider]], [[wine]], milk, chocolate milk, and [[eggnog]]. The player can also place food from crates in the basement of the [[Blue Moon Inn]]. The main courses include chicken, beef, jubbly, nut roast, mushroom wellington, and trout. Side dishes include potatoes, sprouts, cauliflower, broccoli, cabbage, peas, parsnips, carrots, and stuffing.
{{2025 Christmas event}}

{{Cache}} {{External|rs=Seth (historical)|rsc}} {{Infobox NPC |name = Seth |image = [[File:Seth.png|120px]] |release = [[27 February]] [[2002]] |update = Latest RuneScape News (27 February 2002) |removal = [[29 March]] [[2004]] |removalupdate = RS2 Launched! |members = Yes |race = [[Human]] |location = [[Brimhaven]] |gender = Male |options = Talk-to |examine = Slightly fishy smelling. |map = No |id = 4918 |leagueRegion = No }} [[File:Seth chathead.png|left]] '''Seth''' was a certer in ''RuneScape Classic'', who could provide certificates for Lobsters and Swordfish. Most certers were not converted to ''RuneScape 2'' as they were replaced by the [[bank note]] system. However, Seth was included in the RuneScape 2 beta files, as he was classified as an NPC used in the [[Heroes' Quest]]. His stall can still be found in [[Brimhaven]] west of the Agility Arena entrance.
It is unknown whether he was ever actually added to ''RuneScape 2'', or was only in the game files. Regardless, he has never been present in ''Old School RuneScape''.

'''Sethos''' was a [[Menaphites|Menaphite]], who lived during the [[Third Age]]. They were at [[Ullek]], when a [[Zamorak]]ian invasion was approaching the city. They hid a [[Chest (Beneath Cursed Sands)|chest]] containing [[Scabaras]] artefacts outside the city, leaving a [[Stone tablet (Beneath Cursed Sands)|stone tablet]] for [[Akhem]] to recover the chest in case the invasion happened.
{{Beneath Cursed Sands}} [[Category:Characters that do not appear in-game]] [[Category:Characters from the Third Age]]

It is used to distract [[Bouncer (ghost)|Bouncer]] after getting him to low health so the player can kill him at the end of the miniquest.

revision.text: {{Infobox Scenery |name = Sewage water |image = [[File:Sewage water.png|300px]] |release = [[24 January]] [[2024]] |update = Scurrius, the Rat King |members = Yes |location = [[Varrock Sewers]] |options = Cross, Quick-escape |examine = It smells horrible in there. |map = {{Map|name=Sewage water|3288,9867|mapID=-1|mtype=pin}} |id = 14204 }} '''Sewage water''' can be found inside [[Scurrius]]' lair. Players can use the "Cross" or "Quick-escape" option to exit the lair; there will be an approximately 15 second delay after leaving before being able to enter the lair once again.

{{External|rs|rsc}} {{Infobox Scenery |name = Sewer valve |image = [[File:Sewer valve.png|250x250px]] |release = [[15 August]] [[2002]] |update = Sheep and cults |members = Yes |quest = [[Hazeel Cult]] |location = South of [[East Ardougne]] |options = Turn-left, Turn-right |examine = This looks like it can be turned. |map = {{Map|name=Sewer valve|x:2611,y:3242|x:2562,y:3247|x:2572,y:3263|x:2585,y:3245|x:2597,y:3263|plane=0|mapID=0|mtype=pin}} |id = 2844,2845,2846,2847,2848 }} '''Sewer valves''' are water-controlling devices found just south of [[Ardougne]]. They are used in the [[Hazeel Cult]] [[quest]]. There are 5 sewer valves total. Each has a "turn-right" and "turn-left" option.
Just east of the [[Clock Tower (building)|Clock Tower]] is a dungeon entrance. Inside there is a raft. When boarded, this raft goes to different places based on the positions of all 5 sewer valves.
Once boarded, the raft takes you to one of five islands depending on the valves' orientation. The island you land on corresponds with the valve that is incorrect. For example, if the second valve is incorrect, you will land on island two. If the zero valve (the Western-most valve) is incorrect, then the raft will not leave the shore. If all valves are correct, you will land on the fifth island, which is the island leading to the Hazeel Cult's hideout. [[File:Sewer Valve Numbers.png|left|thumb|Sewer Valve Numbers. When a valve is incorrect, you will land on the corresponding numbered island.]]
{{Hazeel Cult}}

{{External|rs}} {{Infobox NPC |name = Shade Spirit |image = [[File:Shade Spirit.png|110px]] |release = [[18 October]] [[2004]] |update = Mortton Shades and Mage Armour |members = Yes |race = [[Ghost]] |location = [[Mort'ton]] pyres |examine = A spirit rising towards eternal peace. |map = No |id = 1278 |leagueRegion = Morytania }} '''Shade Spirits''' are cremated versions of [[Shade (disambiguation)|shade]]s in the [[Shades of Mort'ton minigame]]. They are created by using [[shade remains]] on the [[Funeral Pyre|pyres]] and then lighting them with [[pyre logs]]. The Shade Spirit will float into the air, rewarding the player with [[Prayer]] experience and either a [[shade key]] or [[coins]]. [[File:Shades of Mort'ton - Burning shade remains.gif|frame|left|Burning a pyre and releasing a Shade Spirit]]
{{Shades of Mort'ton (minigame)}} {{Mort'ton}} [[Category:Non-interactive characters]]

{{External|rs}} '''Shade keys''' are used in the [[Shades of Mort'ton (minigame)|Shades of Mort'ton minigame]]. They can be obtained as a reward for cremating a [[Shade (disambiguation)|shade]], and are used to open chests in the [[Shade Catacombs]]. Shade keys come in combinations of 1 of 5 metals, and 1 of 5 colours, with each combination corresponding to 1 of 25 chest types. {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center;" ! ==Metal type and loop colour== The '''type of metal''' the key is made of directly determines the list of potential rewards the player can obtain from the corresponding chest. For example, bronze chests will only contain low-level armour and weapons, such as [[Steel equipment|steel]] or [[Black equipment|black]], while silver chests will yield higher value items, such as [[Mithril equipment|mithril]], [[Adamant equipment|adamant]] or [[rune equipment]]. Each chest has a long list of possible rewards, including [[runes]], [[jewellery]], [[clue scroll]]s, and melee armour and weapons. There is also a chance to receive [[swamp paste]].
The '''colour of the loop''' of the key determines the probabilities of receiving each reward from its list. Keys of "better" colours are more likely to yield better rewards. The order of colours, from worst to best, is red, brown, crimson, black, purple.
In short: all keys of the '''same metal type''' have the '''same reward list'''; the colour of the key only affects the '''probabilities''' of obtaining specific items.
==Trivia== *[[Black key black]] is the only shade key where the loop half and tooth half share the same colour. *The only type of key a player may obtain without gaining [[Prayer]] experience is the bronze variety. *When dropped by shade remain cremation, they will stay on the ground and not be visible by other players for five minutes.

{{External|rs}} {{Otheruses|the quest|the minigame|Shades of Mort'ton (minigame)}} {{Has quick guide}} {{Infobox Quest |name = Shades of Mort'ton |number = 61 |image = [[File:Shades of Mor'ton.png|300px]] |release = [[18 October]] [[2004]] |update = Mortton Shades and Mage Armour |members = Yes |series = None |developer = Tytn H }} '''Shades of Mort'ton''' is a quest that takes place in [[Morytania]]. The town of [[Mort'ton]] is overrun with Shades, and a strange affliction has taken over the townspeople. The player uncovers an old cure for the affliction and must help the village. ==Details== {{Quest details |start = Find the [[Diary (Shades of Mort'ton)|Diary of Herbi Flax]] on a shelf in a house at the village of [[Mort'ton]]. |startmap = 3481,3279 |difficulty = Intermediate |description = The townsfolk of [[Mort'ton]] have some form of strange affliction and the town is full of Shades. Can you find some way to reverse this? |length = Short |requirements = * Completion of the following quests: ** [[Priest in Peril]] * {{SCP|Crafting|20|link=yes}} {{Boostable|yes}} {{Questreqstart|no}} * {{SCP|Herblore|15|link=yes}} {{Boostable|yes}} {{Questreqstart|no}} * {{SCP|Firemaking|5|link=yes}} {{Boostable|Yes}} {{Questreqstart|no}} * Must be able to defeat 5 level-40 [[Loar Shade]]s. * Must be able to survive an onslaught when rebuilding the Temple (Being surrounded by many players makes this much easier). * Access to [[Mort'ton]] |items = * 1000+ [[coins]] (bring plenty of money just in case) * 2 [[Tarromin potion (unf)]] OR 2 [[vials of water]] and 2 [[tarromins]] (both obtainable during the quest) * 2 [[ashes]] *[[Tinderbox]] *[[Logs]] OR an [[axe]] to obtain some * 1 [[hammer]] **Using a [[Flamtaer hammer]] is '''highly recommended''' in case the minigame is unpopulated, as a regular hammer is insufficient to build the temple alone. An additional 13,000 coins (or {{Coins|{{GEP|Flamtaer hammer}}}} on the [[Grand Exchange]]) allows you to buy a [[Flamtaer hammer]] from Razmire. |recommended = * {{SCP|Combat|25|link=yes}} * [[Combat equipment]] * [[Food]] * 1-4 [[Flamtaer bracelet]]s (HIGHLY recommended; the minigame is occasionally unpopulated) * 11 free inventory slots * Fast travel to [[Mort'ton]] to start the quest - [[Mort'ton Teleport]], [[Barrows Teleport]], [[fairy ring]] {{Fairycode|bkr}} and take the [[swamp boaty]], or [[Morytania legs 3]]+ |kills = * 5 [[Loar Shade]]s ''(level 40)'' |leagueRegion = {{LeagueRegion|Morytania}} — location requirement }} ==Walkthrough== {{Map|align=right|zoom=2|x=3482|y=3278|mtype=pin|width=250|height=250|caption=Where to start the quest.}} :'''Note:''' The only nearby bank is unlocked during [[In Aid of the Myreque]]. It is recommended to bring all required items with you on your first visit to Mort'ton. ===Starting the quest=== [[File:Diary (Shades of Mort'ton) detail.png|left|70px]] Head to the most south-western house in Mort'ton and search the shelf on the wall to find a [[Diary (Shades of Mort'ton)|book]]. '''You should also search the [[smashed table (Mort'ton)|smashed table]], as it contains two [[Tarromin]] and [[Rogue's purse]].''' The Tarromin will allow you to create additional potions later on, and you may save the Rogue's purse if you plan to do [[Zogre Flesh Eaters]]. This building also contains a vial spawn in case you didn't bring vials of water with you. You can fill the vials in the sink in the easternmost building. ===Serum 207 and killing shades=== {{Needed|1000+ [[coins]], 2 [[tarromin potion (unf)]] (or 2 [[tarromin]] and 2 [[vials of water]]), 2 [[ashes]], [[food]], [[armour]], and a [[weapon]]|skills={{SCP|Herblore|15}} {{Boostable|yes}} to create [[Serum 207]]}} [[File:Serum 207 (4) detail.png|left|70px]] Reading the book will now allow you to create [[Serum 207]], a potion which may be used on the afflicted in town to '''temporarily''' interact with them. If you don't already have a [[tarromin potion (unf)]], use [[tarromin]] on a [[vial of water]] ({{SCP|Herblore|12}}). Use [[ashes]] on the unfinished potion to create the Serum (also complete your second potion) ({{SCP|Herblore|15}}). :'''Note''': Serum 207 can be bought on the [[Grand Exchange]], but you must make at least one yourself for the purpose of this quest. [[File:Razmire General Store..png|thumb|250px]] Use the Serum on [[Razmire Keelgan]] in the [[general store]]. Ask him what all these shadowy creatures are, and he will tell you they are restless spirits of the dead. He asks you to kill 5 [[Loar Shade]]s (the level 40 green shadows) and collect their [[Loar remains|remains]] so that he may do some experiments on them. :'''Note''': The kills will only count after Razmire has asked you to kill them, and you must collect the remains via killing them. {{mes|That's all five Shades!}} will appear in the chat when you are done. Return to Razmire and use the Serum 207 on Razmire again, and he will take two of the shade remains from you. He then mentions that [[Ulsquire Shauncy]] might also be interested in seeing some shade remains. Before heading to Ulsquire, open the general store through Razmire and buy some [[olive oil]]. Then ask him to open the builders store, and buy 1-2 [[timber beam]], 1-2 [[limestone brick]], and 10-20 [[swamp paste]]. :'''Note''': The supplies may be much more expensive on World 377 (the official Shades of Mor'ton minigame world) due to players buying them up, so consider switching worlds temporarily before buying them. Ulsquire can be found in the house right next to Razmire to the south-east. Give him a dose of Serum 207, and then one of your [[shade remains]]. Talk to him again, and ask what he found out from the remains. Ulsquire believes that the tormented spirits should be put to rest, and jokes about rebuilding the nearby [[Flamtaer|temple]] and experimenting with the sacred flame. Next, ask him what he can tell you about the temple. He will suggest that to rebuild it, you will need the items you have just bought from Razmire. {{Chat option|1What did you find out about the remains?|2What can you tell me about that temple?}} :'''Note''': Make sure you complete the dialogue options with Ulsquire, or interacting with the temple will result in the message {{Mes|You're not quite sure how to fix this}}. ===Repairing the Temple=== {{Main|Shades of Mort'ton (minigame)}} {{needed|[[Hammer]] or [[Flamtaer hammer]], [[food]], [[armour]], [[Weapons|weapon]], [[tinderbox]], [[logs]] or [[axe]], [[loar remains]], [[olive oil]], and 1+ [[Serum 207|doses of Serum 207]] (2+ recommended). Building materials: multiples of [[limestone brick]], [[timber beam]], 5 [[swamp paste]]|recommended=1-2 [[Flamtaer bracelet]]s are recommended|skills={{SCP|Crafting|20}} {{Boostable|yes}} to repair the temple walls, {{SCP|Herblore|15}} {{Boostable|yes}} if choosing to create [[serum 208]]}} [[File:Flaming Fire altar.png|left|70px]] [[File:Flamtaer.png|thumb|250px|The Flamtaer temple when fully repaired with the fire altar lit.]] Now, you must help rebuild the temple located on a small island north-east of the general store, in order to create the sacred oil needed for a pyre funeral. This section of the quest serves as a short introduction to the Shades of Mort'ton [[Shades of Mort'ton (minigame)|minigame]]. It is possible to complete this solo if using several [[Flamtaer bracelet]]'s along with the [[Flamtaer hammer]], but you may consider using the official World 377 dedicated to this minigame to find other players also rebuilding the temple, as this will make the process '''significantly faster'''. In this minigame, players work together to rebuild the temple while under attack from [[Loar Shade]]s. To complete this quest, rebuild the walls around the temple using your hammer and build materials ({{SCP|Crafting|20}}). The [[Flamtaer hammer]] and [[Flamtaer bracelet]] make this process approximately 75% faster (the bracelet degrades after 80 uses). Once fully rebuilt, ignite the flame and then use the [[olive oil]] on it to create [[sacred oil]], provided you have at least 10% Sanctity. Sanctity is earned by your contribution towards repairing or reinforcing the walls, or by killing [[Loar Shades]] (only recommended for high combat levels). :'''Note''': Once you have your sacred oil, it is optional but '''highly recommended''' to use your remaining [[Serum 207]] on the flame with at least 20% Sanctity, to create [[Serum 208]] ({{SCP|Herblore|15}}). This will permanently cure [[Razmire]] and [[Ulsquire]], making them permanently available for dialogue and trade. It may also be used on other [[afflicted]] citizens for a small [[Serum_208#Cure_rewards|reward]]. ===Burning a Shade=== [[File:Shades of Mort'ton - Burning shade remains.gif|thumb|right|250px||The Shade spirit is now free!]] {{Needed|[[Sacred oil]], [[logs]] or [[axe]], [[loar remains]], [[tinderbox]]|skills={{SCP|Firemaking|5}} {{Boostable|yes}} to use pyre logs on the funeral pyre}} If you do not yet have logs, cut down a nearby [[dead tree]]. Use your sacred oil on the [[logs]] to receive a [[pyre logs|pyre log]]. Then, head over to one of the funeral pyres, which are the brown patches on the map west of the General Store. Use the pyre logs on the funeral pyre, followed by the [[Loar remains]]. Light this and you will see a spirit rise from the pyre. ({{SCP|Firemaking|5}}) Collect your reward from the stone pillar next to the pyre and head back to Ulsquire. Speak with him to prompt the end of the quest (use a serum if he has reverted to being afflicted). '''Congratulations, quest complete!''' {{clear}} ==Rewards== {{Quest rewards |name = Shades of Mort'ton |image = [[File:Shades of Mort'ton reward scroll.png|centre]] |qp = 3 |rewards = *{{SCP|Herblore|2,000}} [[Herblore]] experience *{{SCP|Crafting|2,000}} [[Crafting]] experience *Ability to play the [[Shades of Mort'ton (minigame)|Shades of Mort'ton minigame]] *Ability to use the Shades of Mort'ton [[minigame teleport]] *Bonus: If you take the [[Diary (Shades of Mort'ton)|Diary of Herbi Flax]] to the [[Apothecary]] in [[Varrock]], you'll get an extra 335 [[Herblore]] experience (can only be done once). }} ==Transcript== {{Hastranscript|quest}} ==Changes== {{Subject changes header}} {{Subject changes |daterange = 26 January -
25 June 2005 |update = |change = The quest was renamed from "Shades of Mortton" to "Shades of Mort'ton". }} {{Subject changes footer}} {{Shades of Mort'ton}}

revision.text:
{{External|rs}} {{Infobox Location |name = Shadow Dungeon |image = [[File:Shadow Dungeon.png]] |release = [[18 April]] [[2005]] |update = Desert Treasure |members = Yes |floors = 1 |location = [[Kandarin]] |race = Varies |music = [[Path of Peril]] |map = {{Map|mapID=-1|zoom=1|height=175|x=2688|y=5088}} |type = dungeon |leagueRegion = Kandarin }} The '''Shadow Dungeon''' is the [[dungeon]] used during [[Desert Treasure I]], where players fight [[Damis]] to obtain the [[shadow diamond]]. To access the dungeon, players must use the [[Ladder (Shadow Dungeon)|ladder]] east of [[Baxtorian Falls]], near [[Rasolo]]. To be able to see the ladder, players are required to wear the [[ring of visibility]] or the [[ring of shadows]]. If lost, the ring of visibility can be reclaimed from [[Rasolo]] west of the [[Fishing Guild]], or if [[Desert Treasure II]] has been completed, the ring of shadows can be bought from the [[Mysterious Bandit]] at the [[Ancient Vault]] for 75,000 coins.
Outside of the quest, the dungeon is only frequented for potential [[Trasure trails|clue steps]]: *Elite: [[Clue scroll (elite) - Cheer in the Shadow dungeon|Cheer in the Shadow dungeon]] *Master: [[Clue scroll (master) - The far north eastern corner where 1 of 4 was defeated|The far north eastern corner where 1 of 4 was defeated]]
The map of the dungeon shows the location of [[Giant skeleton (Shadow Dungeon)|Giant skeletons]] (G), [[Shadow Hound]]s (S), Damis (2, during Desert Treasure I), and the path to the end of the dungeon where Damis as well as the dig location for the master clue step can be found.
[[File:Shadow Dungeon map.png|300px|thumb|left|The route to get to Damis.]]
==Transportation== The Shadow Dungeon can be found down a [[Ladder (Shadow Dungeon)|ladder]] south-east of [[Baxtorian Falls]]; a [[ring of visibility]] or [[ring of shadows]] must be equipped to see the ladder. The ladder can be found within the fenced area north of the [[moss giant]]s and south of [[Glarial's Tomb]]. These are located slightly west of the [[Fishing Guild]].
{| |{{Map|align=left|2547,3421|r=2|mtype=square|caption=The entrance to the Shadow Dungeon.|width=200|height=200}} |[[File:Shadow Dungeon entrance.png|thumb|left|x200px|The ladder leading to the dungeon, visible whilst having the ring of visibility or ring of shadows equipped.]] |} {{clear|left}}
==Monsters== *[[Giant skeleton (Shadow Dungeon)|Giant skeletons]] - Level 80 *[[Shadow Hound]]s - Level 63 *[[Rat]] - Level 2 *[[Giant rat]] - Levels 3 and 6 *[[Bat]] - Level 6 *[[Giant bat]] - Level 27 *[[Damis]] - Level 103/174 (first and second form, respectively)
The dungeon can be difficult to navigate, as it has a maze-like structure. Once Damis is killed during [[Desert Treasure I]], he will not reappear in the dungeon.
{{Shadow Dungeon}} {{Desert Treasure I}} {{Dungeons}} [[Category:Quest locations]] [[Category:Kandarin]]

{{External|rs}} {{HasTask|Dogs}} {{Infobox Monster |name = Shadow Hound |image = [[File:Shadow Hound.png|150px]] |release = [[18 April]] [[2005]] |update = Desert Treasure |members = Yes |combat = 63 |size = 1 |examine = Looks hungry! |xpbonus = 0 |max hit = 6 |aggressive = Yes |poisonous = No |attack style = [[Stab]] |attack speed = 4 |respawn = 50 |slayxp = 62 |cat = Dogs |assignedby = turael,spria,mazchna |hitpoints = 62 |att = 53 |str = 54 |def = 54 |mage = 1 |range = 1 |attbns = 0 |strbns = 0 |amagic = 0 |mbns = 0 |arange = 0 |rngbns = 0 |dstab = 0 |dslash = 0 |dcrush = 0 |dmagic = 0 |dlight = 0 |dstandard = 0 |dheavy = 0 |poisonresistance = 0 |venomresistance = 0 |immunecannon = No |immunethrall = No |id = 3449 }} [[File:Shadow Dungeon map.png|thumb|The [[safespot]] where a shadow hound can be killed.]] '''Shadow Hounds''' are [[dog]]-like monsters found in the [[Shadow Dungeon]]. They can be accessed by wearing a [[ring of visibility]] during or after the [[Desert Treasure I]] [[quest]] or [[Ring of shadows]] after [[Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire]]. They are seldom killed due to being located in a [[multicombat area]], as well as providing no drops except [[bones]]. As with most monsters in the Shadow Dungeon, they allow other monsters to pass through them. {{Infobox Monster |name = Shadow Keeper |image = [[File:Shadow Keeper.png|150px]] |release = [[26 July]] [[2023]] |update = Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire |members = Yes |combat = 131 |size = 2 |examine = Protector of shadows. |xpbonus = |max hit = 12 |aggressive = Yes |poisonous = No |attack style = [[Slash]] |attack speed = 4 |hitpoints = 100 |att = 140 |str = 110 |def = 100 |mage = 100 |range = 1 |attbns = 0 |strbns = 0 |amagic = 0 |mbns = 0 |arange = 0 |rngbns = 0 |dstab = 0 |dslash = 0 |dcrush = 0 |dmagic = 0 |dlight = 0 |dstandard = 0 |dheavy = 0 |poisonresistance = 100 |venomresistance = 100 |immunecannon = Yes |immunethrall = Yes |freezeresistance = 100 |id = 12248 }} '''Shadow Keepers''' are entities that guard the sealed [[remnant]]s found throughout the [[Shadow Realm]] within the [[Lassar Undercity]]. Using standard melee attacks, it is recommended to place [[shadow blocker]]s next to sealed remnants in the real world so that they can focus on defeating the Shadow Keeper without worrying about their [[sanity]].
Despite their appearance, they are not classified as [[demon]]s.
{{Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire}}
[[Category:Quest monsters]]

{{external|rs}} {{otheruses|the hidden realm|the book|The shadow realm}}
The '''Shadow Realm''' is a realm that is, in some sense, a hidden part of [[Gielinor]] rather than a separate dimension. It forms an invisible layer of reality seemingly spanning the entire world. Objects and people that are inside the Shadow Realm are normally not visible to people outside of it, although it is still possible to see them using a [[ring of visibility]] or a [[ring of shadows]]. Some beings, such as certain [[Gods]] and [[Mahjarrat]], are also able to see things hiding in the Shadow Realm, seemingly without any external aid. [[Dark beast]]s also have a natural connection to the shadows, giving them a greater connection to the Shadow Realm.
Objects from the Shadow Realm are featured in several quests and miniquests such as the entrance to the [[Shadow Dungeon]] in [[Desert Treasure I]], the [[ghostly robes]] in the [[Curse of the Empty Lord]], and the [[shadow sword]] in [[The General's Shadow]]. In addition, the player is able to be present in the Shadow Realm by being targeted to guide the maze during the fight with [[Sotetseg]] in the [[Theatre of Blood]], and while possessing the [[blackstone fragment]] and entering the [[puddle]]s in [[Lassar Undercity]] during and after [[Desert Treasure II]]. Entering the Shadow Realm is also a prominent mechanic in the fight with [[The Whisperer]].
The influence of the Shadow Realm is immense in Lassar's undercity due to the [[Ancient Pillar (Desert Treasure II)|blackstone pillar]], and players who attempt to enter wearing a [[ring of shadows]] will find it immediately slipped off their fingers. Although unconfirmed, the Shadow Realm likely has influence in the [[Cursed Archipelago]], as tendrils similar to the ones in Lassar can be found in its waters, which are known as [[profane waters]]. Identical shadow-black hands can also be seen coming out of the waters beside the ancient forge in [[Grimstone Dungeon]], and in the shadow version of [[Port Piscarilius]] that the [[Judge of Yama (A Kingdom Divided)|Judge of Yama]] takes players to during [[A Kingdom Divided]].
==Gallery== <gallery mode="packed" heights="150" style="text-align:left"> Sotetseg Shadow Realm.png|The Shadow Realm during the Sotetseg fight. Lassar Undercity - Shadow Realm building concept.png|Concept art of the Shadow Realm version of the buildings and objects in the Lassar Undercity. Lassar Undercity Palace (Shadow Realm) concept art.png|Concept art of the Shadow Realm version of the Palace in the Lassar Undercity. Fighting the Judge of Yama.png|The shadow version of Port Piscarilius the Judge of Yama transports the player to. Judge of Yama Shadow Hands.gif|Shadowy hands emerging from the water in the shadow version of Port Piscarilius. Grimstone Dungeon - shadow hands.gif|Shadowy hands emerging from the water in the Grimstone Dungeon. </gallery>
==Trivia== * The [[Shaeded Beast]] appears to be trapped in the Shadow Realm, as it is only visible when wearing a [[ring of visibility]], and it claims that it is trying to find a person it can use as a puppet to help it return to Gielinor. * [[Zombie Pirate (Sailing)|Zombie pirates]] with shadowy hands wrapped around their bodies were present in the [[June 2025 Sailing Beta|Sailing Beta]], which were likely intended to have some connection to the Shadow Realm, though they did not make it into the final release of [[Sailing]]. <!--see trivia on their page for more details that basically confirm this-->

{{External|rs}} {{Has quick guide}} {{Infobox Quest |name = Shadow of the Storm |number = 91 |image = [[File:Shadow of the Storm.png|300px]] |release = [[14 November]] [[2005]] |update = Shadow of the Storm |members = Yes |series = [[Quests/Series#Demon Slayer|Demon Slayer]], #2 |developer = John A }} '''Shadow of the Storm''' is a quest that continues the plot of [[Demon Slayer]]. It involves the villain [[Denath]] once more, as well as his group of followers attempting to summon a dangerous demon named [[Agrith-Naar]].
==Details== {{Quest details |start = Speak to [[Father Reen]], south of [[Al Kharid]] bank. |startmap = 3271,3158 |difficulty = Intermediate |description = A sinister group of dark wizards is attempting to summon Agrith-Naar, a demon of exceptional mystical power. Rather than try to prevent them, a Saradominist priest asks the player to help summon the demon and then kill it once and for all.
But all is not as it seems... |length = Medium |requirements = *{{SCP|Crafting|30|link=yes}} {{Boostable|yes}} {{Questreqstart|}} *Completion of the following quests: **[[The Golem]] **[[Demon Slayer]] *The ability to defeat a level 100 demon |items = *[[Silverlight]] (obtainable at start of quest) *[[Strange implement]] (obtainable during quest) *Any black outfit (minimum of 3 pieces, see [[Shadow_of_the_Storm#Starting_Out|below]] for the allowed gear — the dyed [[Silverlight]] '''does not''' count as a piece of black clothing) **'''Note:''' You can make a [[black desert robe]] and [[black desert shirt|shirt]] during the quest if you brought a [[desert robe]] and [[desert shirt|shirt]] *[[Black dye]] (from grinding a black mushroom using a pestle and mortar alongside a vial) *[[Silver bar]] *Means to enter the desert (such as the [[Shantay pass (item)|Shantay pass]], [[Desert amulet 2]], [[Teleport tablets]] or [[Teleport scrolls|scrolls]], [[Fairy rings]] or the [[Pharaoh's sceptre]]) |kills = [[Agrith-Naar]] ''(level 100)'' |recommended = *{{SCP|Combat|50|link=yes}} *Fast travel to Al Kharid to start the quest ([[amulet of glory]] or [[ring of dueling]]) *Fast travel to Uzer ([[necklace of passage]] to Eagles' Eyrie, [[Fairy Rings]] to {{fairycode|dlq}} or using the [[magic carpet]] transport) *[[Food]] and [[armour]] to defeat a level 100 demon *2 [[waterskin]]s *[[Chisel]] and [[hammer]] (optional to obtain several gems from the throne, unless already taken during [[The Golem]]) |leagueRegion = <poem> Unlocking {{LeagueRegion|Desert}} {{okay}} will auto-complete the quest </poem> }}
==Walkthrough== {{Map|name=Father Reen|x=3272|y=3159|r=4|mtype=square|align=right|width=220|height=220|caption=The quest's start point.}} ===Starting Out=== {{Needed|[[Silverlight]], 3 items of black clothing (see below), transport to the [[Ruins of Uzer]] (e.g. [[necklace of passage]]; or [[ring of dueling]], [[Shantay pass (item)|Shantay pass]] and 200 [[coins]])}}
Talk to [[Father Reen]], south of [[Al Kharid]] bank. If you do not have a regular [[Silverlight]], he will give you an uncoloured Silverlight free of charge. '''If you already have a dyed Silverlight, bank the extra Silverlight. If this dialogue is missed, Silverlight can still be obtained at other points in the quest by speaking to him.'''
After you start, travel to the [[Ruins of Uzer]] (you can enter the desert via the [[Shantay Pass]] and use the [[magic carpet]], rub a [[necklace of passage]] to Eagles' Eyrie and run south-east or travel with [[fairy ring|fairy rings]] to {{Fairycode|DLQ}} and run north-east). Be sure to bring your Silverlight with you since you won't be able to continue without it. After arriving in Uzer, talk to [[Father Badden]] - be sure to talk to him about all your options. If you haven't already, pick a black mushroom. Afterwards, enter the dungeon.
When you try to enter the demon's lair, [[Evil Dave]] won't let you by because you aren't evil enough. You need to wear at least three items of black clothing. There are several ways to achieve this, including: [[File:Shadow of the Storm - black mushrooms.png|thumb|220px|A black mushroom near the entrance.]]
*Dyeing a [[desert shirt]] and a [[desert robe]] black by picking a [[black mushroom]] outside of the dungeon and crafting it into [[black dye]] with a [[vial]] and [[pestle and mortar]], for two of the three items (does not work on the [[desert boots]]). *Wearing any three [[black armour]] items. The [[black gloves]] available from the [[Culinaromancer's Chest]] also function as a black armour item (although this quest must be completed in order to finish the [[Freeing Evil Dave|Evil Dave part]] of Recipe for Disaster) '''Note:''' Wearing heraldic or trimmed black armour items will not be accepted by Evil Dave. *Wearing a black [[priest gown]] purchased from the [[Thessalia|clothing vendor]] in [[Varrock]]. *Wearing [[Mystic robes#Dark|dark mystic robes]]. *Wearing [[ghostly robes]] from the [[Curse of the Empty Lord]] miniquest. *Wearing [[shade robes]]. *Wearing [[black dragonhide armour]]. *Wearing the [[Antisanta outfit]]. *Wearing a [[black cape]], [[black partyhat]], [[black santa hat]], [[black h'ween mask]], [[black dragon mask]], and/or a [[black unicorn mask]] *Wearing black [[wizard robes]], including either trimmed varieties (blue varieties can be dyed with [[Black dye]]). *Wearing a [[graceful outfit]] which has been recoloured using [[dark dye]].
{| class="mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" !The following items are '''not''' considered "evil" by Evil Dave: |- | *[[Ahrim the Blighted's equipment|Ahrim's robes]] *[[Aranea boots]] *[[Banshee top|Banshee Top]] / [[Banshee robe|Robe]] *[[Black beret]] *[[Black boater]] *[[Black cavalier]] *[[Black defender]] *[[Black Elegant Shirt]] *[[Black headband]] *[[Black knife]] *[[Black leprechaun hat]] *[[Black mask]] *[[Black naval set|Black naval clothing]] *[[Black satchel]] *[[Black spiky vambraces]] *[[Bloodbark armour]] *[[Cape of skulls]] *[[Dagon'hai robes|Dagon'hai Robes]] *[[Evil chicken outfit]] *[[Eyepatch]] *[[Gloves of silence]] *[[Khazard helmet]] / [[Khazard armour|armour]] *[[Mime boots]] *[[Obsidian cape]] *[[Robes of darkness]] *[[Robes of Ruin|Robes of ruin]] *[[Rogue equipment]] *[[Shayzien equipment|Shayzien Equipment]] *[[Void knight equipment]] *[[Vyrewatch clothing]] *[[Zamorak Cape|Zamorak cape]] |}
You also need to dye your Silverlight black using black dye from the same black mushrooms inside the dungeon (this doesn't count as an "evil" item).
:'''Note:''' You cannot proceed with the quest if you have a normal Silverlight alongside a dyed Silverlight.
Equip your three black items, then tell Evil Dave you want to join the group, and he will let you through the portal. Evil Dave will take you to the leader of the group, [[Denath]]. He will tell you that he needs your help to summon [[Agrith-Naar]], since [[Josef]] left. '''He will tell you the incantation to use, which is different for everyone, so you need to write it down.''' In case you forget the incantation, you can read the [[Demonic tome|tome]] you'll find later on and cite the phrase in it backwards.
===The Ritual=== {{Needed|[[Silver bar]], [[strange implement]] (optional), [[ring of dueling]] or 200 [[coins]] (optional), [[Shantay pass (item)|Shantay pass]] and 200 [[coins]], or [[necklace of passage]] (optional), and 3 free inventory spaces}}
'''Optional''': Using a chisel and hammer on the demon's throne will give the player six cut gems: two [[Sapphire|sapphires]], two [[Ruby|rubies]] and two [[Emerald|emeralds]]. While this can be done during [[The Golem]] quest, it can alternatively be completed during this quest.[[File:Shadow of the Storm - Evil Dave introduces player.png|thumb|220px|Evil Dave introduces their newest dark wizard, you, to Denath.]] Talk to [[Jennifer]] to get a [[demonic sigil mould]]. Then, talk to [[Matthew]] about Josef. He will tell you to find the book that [[Josef]] dropped in order to defeat the demon. Talk to the [[clay golem]] and ask if it knows what happened last night; it will explain that Denath killed Josef, but not before Josef hid the book in the kiln outside. '''You must talk to the golem before you can search the kiln!'''
In Uzer, search the kilns that are outside until you find a [[Demonic Tome]]. There are two close by, and two further away. One is north of the magic carpet, and the other is east of the temple. There are '''4''' kilns in total.
Go to any furnace (such as the furnace in [[Lumbridge]] or in [[Al Kharid|Al Kharid.]] Fairy Ring {{fairycode|dkr}} to Edgeville furnace is fastest), and make a [[demonic sigil]] with your [[silver bar]]. With the sigil, you will be able to chant the incantation with the group.
'''You no longer need your black equipment to enter the portal. If you need to gear up for the fight, save a trip and bring what you need.''' '''You will need 3 free inventory slots.'''[[File:Shadow of the Storm - Matthew smells trouble.png|thumb|left|Matthew begins to suspect something evil is afoot.]] Read the book and return through the portal, then hand Matthew the book. Strangely enough, the incantation for summoning the demon that's written in the book is backwards to the one that Denath told you to say. This is due to the fact that the incantation in the book is one to summon the demon (forward) while the one Denath told you was to return him back to the demon plane (backwards).[[File:Shadow of the Storm - Denath teleports away.png|thumb|220px|Denath walks into the centre of the circle, teleporting away!]] When you have finished, Denath will call you over to stand next to him and lead the incantation. Using your sigil, chant it in the order that he told you (if you have forgotten, it's written in the book, but backwards). After the portal is opened, instead of the demon coming out of it, Denath will walk into it and disappear. It turns out Denath was Agrith-Naar all along, and you actually desummoned him by saying the incantation ''backwards'', as he intended.
This demon becomes much more powerful in his own dimension, so you need to resummon him and defeat him. Pick up the sigil that Denath dropped '''(if you don't, you will have to make another one)'''. Alternatively, it is possible to have Tanya drop two sigils by returning to demonic realm immediately after chasing her through the portal (see below). If done correctly, she will drop two sets of sigils and bones.
[[Evil Dave]], [[Eric]], and [[Tanya]] will have run away, so chase after them through the portal. Tanya is killed by ghosts, so take her sigil as well. Eric is killed by a falling stone. Convince Evil Dave to return to the lair, and he will give you Eric's sigil. Leave the dungeon and talk to [[Father Badden]] and [[Father Reen]]. Convince them to help with the ritual and give them both a sigil. You need one more individual to complete the incanctation, so talk to the [[Clay Golem]]. However, he was programmed to never help summon demons. Use the [[strange implement]] (can be found in the lair) on him to take out the scroll about demon rituals. Speak to the golem again and he will agree to help you. [[File:Shadow of the Storm - Tanya is killed.png|thumb|220px|Tanya is killed by ghosts during her attempt to flee.]]
===The Final Fight=== {{Needed|[[Silverlight]], [[demonic sigil]], equipment to defeat [[Agrith Naar|Agrith-Naar]] (level 100)}} {{Instance}}
Return to the demon's lair, enter the portal and talk to Matthew to get everyone to stand in the circle. Chant the incantation with your sigil, this time in the order that you read in the book (the opposite order that you chanted it in last time). Agrith-Naar will immediately appear and turn to Matthew, killing him in the belief that he started the ritual. Your character will then say that you commenced it, prompting the demon to attack you.
'''Note:''' You cannot use a [[Dwarf multicannon]] during the bossfight, as you'll get a message saying "''Some kind of demonic magic prevents the cannon from functioning".'' [[File:Shadow of the Storm - Agrith-Naar resummoned.png|thumb|220px|Agrith-Naar is resummoned!]]
[[Agrith Naar|Agrith-Naar]] is a level 100 [[Demons|demon]] who remains in the same position throughout the fight. He uses both [[Melee]] and [[Fire Blast]] depending on where you are and what [[Protection prayers]] you have activated. He uses melee by default, but switches to Fire Blast if you activate [[Protect from Melee]] or walk out of range. If you walk out of melee range and activate [[Protect from Magic]], he will cast [[Telekinetic Grab]] to teleport you next to him. '''''Note:''' You can potentially have full protection by using Protect from Magic and [[flinching]] from two squares away, running out of melee range immediately after he casts Telekinetic Grab. However this method requires precise timing and is not simple to pull off.'' [[File:Fighting Agrith-Naar.png|thumb|240px|The player battles Agrith-Naar.]] '''You must hit the final blow with Silverlight in order to win the fight.''' If Agrith-Naar is reduced to zero hit-points through any other method, a message will appear stating "''You can't kill Agrith-Naar except with Silverlight.''" and his health will be restored to 12. '''''Note:''' If timed well, it is however possible to deal the last blow with any other weapon than the Silverlight, as long as you stand next to the boss and swap back to the Silverlight right before the last hit is registered.''
'''{{Colour|red|Warning}}:''' If you are [[flinching]] the boss with the Silverlight and move behind a pillar or torch before the final blow is registered (between the XP drop and the damage being dealt), then it will '''not''' count, and Agrith-Naar will recover a small bit of health.
Once the demon is dead, your [[Silverlight]] will have been merged with the demon's blood into a stronger weapon, the [[Darklight]]. '''''Note:''' If your prayer runs out during the message or you cancel the chat, un-equipping Darklight will trigger the final dialogue to complete the quest.''
'''Congratulations, quest complete!'''
==Rewards== {{Quest rewards |name = Shadow of the Storm |image = [[File:Shadow of the Storm reward scroll.png|centre]] |qp = 1 |rewards = *10,000 [[experience]] in any [[combat]] skill other than [[Prayer]]. *[[Silverlight]] turns into the [[Darklight]] sword - it has a [[special attack]] and is even more powerful against [[demon]]s. It costs slightly more to replace. *Six cut gems: two [[sapphire]]s, two [[rubies]] and two [[emerald]]s, if you use a hammer and chisel on the demon's throne and had not yet removed them during [[The Golem]].
Unlocks: * [[Agrith-Naar]] accessible in the [[Nightmare Zone]]. }}
==Required for completing== Completion of Shadow of the Storm is required for the following: * [[Recipe for Disaster]] ([[Recipe for Disaster/Freeing Evil Dave|Freeing Evil Dave]])
==Transcript== {{hastranscript|Quest}}
==Trivia== *When [[Patrick]] says he will get a small piece of coloured paper, he is referring to a [[partyhat]]. At the time this quest was released during RS2, party hats were some of the rarest and most valuable items in the game. *If you removed the [[gems]] from the throne during [[The Golem]], [[Evil Dave]] will complain that the lack of gems diminishes the evil ambience of the throne room. *If you talk to [[Eric]] and walk away before he's finished talking, he will do the "[[Angry]]" emote and say "Don't ignore me!" *If you talk to [[Tanya]] and use the dialogue choice, "Oh?", she will say, "I shall be a dark queen over all Gielinor! All shall love me and despair!" This line paraphrases a monologue delivered by the character {{WP|Galadriel}} in ''The Fellowship of the Ring''. *If you speak with the rug merchant while the sandstorm is brewing outside the temple, he will still allow travel, exclaiming "Ali Morrisane's carpet fleet flies in any weather" **If you tell him you have some more questions for him during the sandstorm, there is an option to ask if he would participate in the demon summoning. If this option is selected, he refuses, saying he can't leave the rugs alone in the sandstorm or they might fly off. *When you question the [[clay golem]] as to why [[Father Badden]] despises him so much, the golem replies, "He should know that I could never hurt him. The first command in a golem's mind is that it cannot allow a human being to come to harm." This is a reference to Isaac Asimov's First [[wikipedia:Three Laws of Robotics|Law of Robotics]]. *Prior to a patch, it was possible to use the [[Silverlight]] sword acquired at the beginning of the quest to complete [[Demon Slayer]] in under a minute, by skipping a portion of the quest where you must collect keys. This was patched on November 28th, 2018. *After completing the quest, Evil Dave says "I'm not going to try to be evil any more. From now on I'm going to be good!" *Evil Dave will not present the player with the challenge clue for the hard anagram clue "VEIL VEDA" while he is in the ruins of Uzer.
{{Shadow of the Storm}}

{{External|rs}} '''Shadow spells''' are one of four types of [[Ancient Magicks]] combat spells. In addition to dealing damage, they have a chance to lower the target's [[Attack]] level if it has not already been drained. If cast using the [[shadow ancient sceptre]], they will also lower the target's Strength and Defence levels if they have not already been drained. The level drain effect is also capable of lowering up to nine targets in a 3x3 grid around its primary target, just like the other additional effects of [[Ancient Magicks|ancient magicks]], on multi-target damaging [[Magic]] spells ([[Burst spells|burst]] and [[Barrage spells|barrage]]). Shadow spells may refer to: {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center;" !Icon ![[Mobile]]
icon !Spell !Level !Runes !Base XP !Max damage
(without bonuses) !Target's Attack
reduced !Target's Attack, Strength,
and Defence reducedOnly when using the [[shadow ancient sceptre]]. Using any other variant of the [[ancient sceptre]] will only reduce the target's attack level by this amount. |- |[[File:Shadow Rush.png]] |[[File:Shadow Rush icon (mobile).png]] |[[Shadow Rush]] |{{SCP|Magic|52}} |{{RuneReq|Soul=1|Death=2|Chaos=2|Air=1}} |31 |14 | rowspan="2" |10% | rowspan="2" |11% |- |[[File:Shadow Burst.png]] |[[File:Shadow Burst icon (mobile).png]] |[[Shadow Burst]] |{{SCP|Magic|64}} |{{RuneReq|Soul=2|Chaos=4|Air=1|Death=2}} |37 |18 |- |[[File:Shadow Blitz.png]] |[[File:Shadow Blitz icon (mobile).png]] |[[Shadow Blitz]] |{{SCP|Magic|76}} |{{RuneReq|Soul=2|Blood=2|Air=2|Death=2}} |43 |24 | rowspan="2" |15% | rowspan="2" |16.5% |- |[[File:Shadow Barrage.png]] |[[File:Shadow Barrage icon (mobile).png]] |[[Shadow Barrage]] |{{SCP|Magic|88}} |{{RuneReq|Air=4|Soul=3|Blood=2|Death=4}} |49 |28 |} {{Reflist}} ===Main uses=== Shadow spells are used in the fight against the [[Abyssal Sire]] during the first phase, to disorientate it so that the [[respiratory system]]s can be damaged. Shadow spells are also used to stun [[the Leviathan]], allowing the player to attack it from behind for extra damage and resetting its attack speed. ==Gallery== Shadow Rush.gif|Shadow Rush Shadow Burst.gif|Shadow Burst Shadow Blitz.gif|Shadow Blitz Shadow Barrage.gif|Shadow Barrage {{Ancient Magicks}} [[Category:Spells]] [[Category:Members' spells]]
