revision.text:
'''Shipbuilding''' is a feature in [[Sailing]] where players can customise a [[boat]] with different types of components and [[facilities]]. It is performed at the [[Shipyard]].
==Ships== Upon completing the [[Pandemonium]] quest, players unlock the [[raft]]. Each upgrade requires a certain [[Sailing]] and [[Construction]] level which can be boosted, including using the [[crystal saw]]. Additional ships can be purchased from [[shipwright]]s, provided the required Sailing level is met.
The raft includes a customisable hull, steering, mast and sails, along with one [[facility hotspot]] and a two-player capacity. At level 15 Sailing, players can unlock the [[skiff]]. A skiff includes a customisable keel, hull, mast and sails, and steering, along with four facility hotspots and capacity for two crewmates and five players. At level 50 Sailing, players can unlock the [[sloop]], which features eight facility hotspots and has capacity for five crewmates and ten players.
===Core boat parts=== Each boat comes with a set of core boat parts, starting with the lowest level. Core boat parts can be changed by using the [[boat schematics]] board. These parts affect the boat's stats and performance and are: * The [[hull]], which affects the ship's hitpoints and speed. * The [[helm]], with higher tier helms giving the ship more resistance to rapids. * The [[mast and sails]], which make the ship accelerate faster and increase the duration of speed boosts from [[Sailing#Ship navigation|wind]]. * The [[keel]], which gives the ship more health and armour. Note: the [[raft]] does not have a keel and cannot be equipped with one. * The [[eternal brazier]], which enables the player to safely traverse the icy seas in the [[Northern Ocean]].
[[Flags]], [[boat paint|trims]] and [[sail patterns]] are also considered core boat parts, but are purely cosmetic.
===Facilities=== {{main|Facilities}} Players can customise their ship, depending on the type of ship and their Sailing and Construction level. Players can build facilities such as [[cargo hold]]s, [[Cannon (Sailing)|cannons]], [[salvaging hook]]s, [[trawling net]]s, and other types of stations as long as they have a [[hammer]], a [[saw]], and the required materials in their inventory.
===Shipwright assistance=== If the player has the required Sailing level, but does not have the required Construction level, a [[shipwright]] can be paid a fee to construct some core boat parts and facilities, up to and including mahogany and mithril. The parts and facilities that the shipwright can build are: * [[Keel]] * [[Hull]] * [[Mast and sails]] * [[Helm]] * [[Cargo hold]] * [[Cannon (Sailing)|Cannon]] * [[Salvaging hook]]
===Ship hazards=== {{main|Sailing_hazards}} '''Sailing hazards''' are dangerous effects that can be encountered in the ocean while [[Sailing]]. When completing a [[sea charting]] task, if there are hazards in the area the task will give a warning about them. If the player enters a hazardous area without adequate protection, any crewmembers operating ship facilities will "panic", cancelling their current orders and will not respond to the player's commands until the ship is out of the hazard zone. Additionally, the player's ship is significantly slowed. Some hazards can be prevented or mitigated through having better equipment on the player's ship.
==Multiple boats== At level 15, 50, 78, and 91, players unlock the ability to have additional boats, up to 2, 3, 4, and 5 respectively. This allows players to have multiple boats suited for different purposes at sea.
The suggested arrangements listed below are suitable for high-level players. Because many components have a linear upgrade progression, lower-level players or ironmen can downgrade any chosen component to suit their needs and abilities.
<tabber> |-|Salvaging = {{Boat |caption = High-level salvaging sloop |float = right |type = sloop |sail = Ironwood |cargo = Rosewood |hull = Camphor |keel = Adamant |helm = Adamant |Dragon salvaging hook | Dragon salvaging hook |Crystal extractor |Salvaging station |Teleport focus |Kraken ink stout || |Horizon's lure|Whirlpool surprise|Wind catcher }} A '''high-level''' salvaging [[sloop]] build consists of at least:
* Highest level [[cargo hold]] ([[Rosewood cargo hold|rosewood]] or [[Ironwood cargo hold|ironwood]]) * Two [[salvaging hook]]s ([[Dragon salvaging hook|dragon]] or [[Rune salvaging hook|rune]]) * One [[Salvaging station (facility)|salvaging station]] * A [[crystal extractor]] for additional experience, preferably placed opposite the [[cargo hold]] and [[Salvaging station (facility)|salvaging station]]. This placement allows access both when salvaging, and when sorting salvage. * Two [[Keg (facility)|kegs]] filled with: ** [[Horizon's lure]] for 2.5% extra experience ** [[Whirlpool surprise]] for an invisible +2 Sailing boost when manually salvaging * An [[adamant keel]] to access [[Barracuda salvage]] in [[crystal-flecked waters]]. Salvaging in these waters will boost the amount of [[crystal shards]] extracted by the [[crystal extractor]] * An [[adamant helm]] to access [[mercenary shipwreck]]s and [[merchant shipwreck]]s in the [[Southern Expanse]] * An [[eternal brazier]] to access [[Fremennik shipwreck]]s and [[merchant shipwreck]]s in the [[Northern Ocean]] * Several optional upgrades to improve trips from and to salvaging spots: ** A [[wind catcher]] for holding/storing wind motes ** A [[Camphor hull|camphor]] or [[rosewood hull]] (an [[ironwood hull]] does not provide additional speed so is not necessary for salvaging) ** An [[ironwood mast and cotton sails]] for longer speed boost duration ** A [[Keg (facility)|keg]] filled with [[Kraken ink stout]] for more frequent [[ocean encounters]]. * Crew: [[Cabin Boy Jenkins (ghost)|Cabin Boy Jenkins]] and [[Jolly Jim]] for their [[Crew Management#Deckhandiness|deckhandiness]]
|-|Trawling = {{Boat |caption = Maxed trawling sloop |float = right |sail = Ironwood |cargo = Rosewood |hull = Rosewood |keel = Rune |helm = Rune |Cotton trawling net|Cotton trawling net |Chum station|Crystal extractor |Fathom pearl|Kraken ink stout || |Gale catcher|Trawler's trust |Teleport focus }} A '''high-level''' [[deep sea trawling]]-focused [[sloop]] setup may consist of the following: * Best available [[hull]] for speed and survivability. Some shoals such as [[marlin shoal]]s require a [[rosewood hull]] to always keep up with it. * Best available [[mast and sails]] for additional speed boost duration. Upgrades above the [[camphor mast and canvas sails]] are less important than the hull, because this only slightly affects the speed boost duration. * Moderate to best available [[keel]] for additional survivability (there are no shoals in [[crystal-flecked waters]], so [[adamant keel]] or better is not a hard requirement). Some shoals come to a rest near aggressive monsters, so additional damage resistance is very helpful. * An [[adamant helm]] or better for trawling in [[tangled kelp]] regions, or a [[rune helm]] to utilize [[powerful rapids]] * An [[eternal brazier]] for trawling in the [[Northern Ocean]] * Best available [[cargo hold]] for maximum storage * A [[Keg (facility)|keg]] filled with [[Trawler's trust]] for an extra 5% catch rate while trawling ** Optionally, kegs with [[Horizon's lure]] and [[Kraken ink stout]] can be added to slightly boost Sailing experience, and increase the number of ocean encounters. * Two of the best available [[trawling net]]s. The port side (left) one is for the crewmember, the starboard side (right) one is for the player. This is to allow the player to open the cargo hold with a single click (which is blocked while operating the port side trawling net). * Optionally, a [[fathom stone]], or the superior [[fathom pearl]] if available. Because shoals follow a consistent pattern, this can also be left off the boat, which will only affect the time to initially find the shoal. * An [[advanced chum station]], or the superior [[chum spreader]] * A [[crystal extractor]] next to one of the trawling nets and diagonally opposite the [[cargo hold]] for additional Sailing experience while trawling * A [[gale catcher]] (or [[wind catcher]]) to gain speed boosts while chasing shoals * Crew: [[Cabin Boy Jenkins (ghost)|Cabin Boy Jenkins]] and/or [[Jolly Jim]] at the nets, and either [[Spotter Virginia]] or [[Sailor Jakob]] on helm. |-|Combat = {{Boat |caption = High-level Combat sloop |float = right |sail = Ironwood |cargo = Ironwood |hull = Rosewood |keel = Dragon |helm = Adamant || |Bosun's workbench|Horizon's lure |Crystal extractor|Dragon cannon |Ballistic attractor|Dragon cannon |Gale catcher|Perildance bitter |Teleport focus }} A suggested combat-focused build on a boat may consist of the following: * One or two of your best available [[Cannon (Sailing)|cannons]] * The best available [[keel]] for decreased damage from monsters * The best available [[hull]] for improved defence against monsters * A decent [[cargo hold]] for storing [[repair kits]] * A [[Keg (facility)|Keg]] filled with [[Perildance bitter]] to boost the cannons' maximum hit by +1. ** Optionally, a keg with [[Horizon's lure]] or [[Kraken ink stout]] can be added to slightly boost Sailing experience, or increase the number of ocean encounters. * An [[eternal brazier]] to be able to access the [[Northern Ocean]], where [[narwhal]]s and [[vampyre kraken]]s can be found * [[Bosun's workbench]], for automatic boat repairs * Optionally, a [[crystal extractor]] for additional sailing experience and [[Crystal shard]]s. * Optionally, a skilling facility ([[salvaging hook]] or [[trawling net]]) for use when not in combat. * Crew: [[Oarswoman Olga]] and [[Jittery Jim]] to man your best available cannons, and have [[Cabin Boy Jenkins (ghost)|Cabin Boy Jenkins]] or [[Jolly Jim]] to repair the boat. Shoot monsters using your best ranged or magic weapon while leaving the two cannons to crewmates. {{clear|right}} |-|Trawling + Combat = {{Boat |caption = Maxed Trawling / combat sloop |float = right |sail = Ironwood |cargo = Rosewood |hull = Rosewood |keel = Dragon |helm = Rune |Cotton trawling net|Cotton trawling net |Chum station|Crystal extractor |Gale catcher|Dragon cannon |Ballistic attractor|Dragon cannon |Perildance bitter|Teleport focus |Fathom pearl }} When desired, significant cost can be saved on having multiple boats, by creating a boat layout that serves multiple different purposes. Because both the trawling and combat builds shown above are filled up with optional facilities (kegs and the [[fathom pearl]]), it is possible to combine these boat builds into a single one. Such a build would use the following: * The best possible [[keel]] for additional survivability * The best possible [[hull]] for survivability and speed * A [[camphor mast and canvas sails]] or better, for improved speed boosts * The best available [[cargo hold]] to store trawled fish * An [[eternal brazier]] to access [[marlin shoal]]s and [[vampyre kraken]]s * An [[adamant helm]] or better for trawling in [[tangled kelp]] regions, or a [[rune helm]] to utilize [[powerful rapids]] * Two [[cotton trawling net]]s. The port side (left) one is for the crewmember, the starboard side (right) one is for the player. This is to allow the player to open the cargo hold with a single click (which is blocked while operating the port side trawling net). * A [[chum spreader]] or [[advanced chum station]] * A [[crystal extractor]] diagonally opposite the [[cargo hold]] and next to one of the trawling nets, for use while trawling * Two of the best available [[Cannon (Sailing)|cannons]] * A [[gale catcher]] or [[wind catcher]] * A [[Ballistic attractor]] * A [[Keg (facility)|kegs]] filled with [[Perildance bitter]] or [[Trawler's trust]], to boost both trawling and combat. Replace the contents whenever switching activities. * A [[Teleport focus (facility)|teleport focus]] for easier/cheaper transportation around the world * The final slot (and/or one of the two kegs) can be filled with either of the following: ** A [[fathom pearl]] or [[fathom stone]] for easier locating of shoals ** A second keg with the other type of beer, for easier switching between activities. * Crew: Choose either [[Oarswoman Olga]] and [[Jittery Jim]] (combat), or [[Cabin Boy Jenkins (ghost)|Cabin Boy Jenkins]] and [[Jolly Jim]] (trawling), plus either [[Spotter Virginia]] or [[Sailor Jakob]] on the helm. Additionally, have either [[Cabin Boy Jenkins (ghost)|Cabin Boy Jenkins]] or [[Jolly Jim]] do the repairs if the boat gets damaged. |-|Salvaging + Combat = {{Boat |caption = Maxed Salvaging / combat sloop |float = right |sail = Ironwood |cargo = Rosewood |hull = Rosewood |keel = Dragon |helm = Adamant |Dragon salvaging hook|Dragon salvaging hook |Crystal extractor|Salvaging station |Teleport focus|Dragon cannon |Ballistic attractor|Dragon cannon |Perildance bitter|Horizon's lure |Gale catcher }} When desired, significant cost can be saved on having multiple boats, by creating a boat layout that serves multiple different purposes. Because the salvaging build has fewer related facilities than the Trawling, it can be easier to combine with combat than Trawling. However, the keg options synergise better with Salvaging than Trawling. Such a build would use the following: * The best possible [[keel]] for additional survivability * The best possible [[hull]] for survivability and speed * A [[camphor mast and canvas sails]] or better, for improved speed boosts * The best available [[cargo hold]] to store salvage * An [[eternal brazier]] to access [[vampyre kraken]]s, [[Fremennik shipwreck]]s, and [[merchant shipwreck]]s in the [[Northern Ocean]] * An [[adamant keel]] to access [[Barracuda salvage]] in [[crystal-flecked waters]]. Salvaging in these waters will boost the amount of [[crystal shards]] extracted by the [[crystal extractor]] * An [[adamant helm]] or better to access [[mercenary shipwreck]]s and [[merchant shipwreck]]s in the [[Southern Expanse]] * Two [[salvaging hook]]s ([[Dragon salvaging hook|dragon]] or [[Rune salvaging hook|rune]]) * A [[crystal extractor]] beside the port side salvaging hook (the side with the [[cargo hold]], for use while salvaging) * A [[Salvaging station (facility)|salvaging station]] on the starboard side, across from the crystal extractor * Two of the best available [[Cannon (Sailing)|cannons]] * A [[gale catcher]] or [[wind catcher]] * A [[Ballistic attractor]] * Two [[Keg (facility)|kegs]] filled with [[Perildance bitter]] and [[Horizon's lure]]. * The final slot can be filled with either of the following: ** A [[Keg (facility)|keg]] filled with [[Whirlpool surprise]] for an invisible +2 Sailing boost when manually salvaging ** A [[Teleport focus (facility)|teleport focus]] for easier/cheaper transportation around the world * Crew: Choose either [[Oarswoman Olga]] and [[Jittery Jim]] (combat), or [[Cabin Boy Jenkins (ghost)|Cabin Boy Jenkins]] and [[Jolly Jim]] (salvaging), plus either [[Spotter Virginia]] or [[Sailor Jakob]] on the helm. Additionally, have either [[Cabin Boy Jenkins (ghost)|Cabin Boy Jenkins]] or [[Jolly Jim]] do the repairs if the boat gets damaged. |-|Barracuda Trials + Courier = {{Boat |caption = Maxed trial/courier skiff |float = right |type = skiff |sail = Rosewood |hull = Rosewood |helm = Adamant |keel = Adamant | ||Horizon's lure |Gale catcher |Crystal extractor |flag = Crystal glider's }} While doing [[courier tasks]], the type of boat used does not limit the number of crewmembers that can help carry cargo to and from ports. Because of this, the more manoeuvrable skiff is preferred over sloops when doing courier tasks, to be able to squeeze through tighter gaps to use [[rapids]]. This can be combined very well with the Barracuda trial skiff. This type of setup consists of the following: * Best available [[hull]] for speed * Best available [[mast and sails]] for acceleration and speed boost duration * Best available [[helm]] to utilize rapids * At least an [[Adamant keel]] to access [[Crystal-flecked waters]] for the elven ports and [[The Gwenith Glide]] * An [[Innoculation station|innoculation<sup>[''sic''<nowiki>]</nowiki></sup> station]] for [[Backwater]] [[fetid waters]] resistance at [[The Jubbly Jive]] * A [[gale catcher]] (or [[wind catcher]]) for releasing wind motes * A [[Keg (facility)|keg]] filled with [[horizon's lure]] for additional experience. ** If horizon's lure is not unlocked, fill it with [[kraken ink stout]] instead for more frequent [[Ocean encounters]] (including [[strong winds]] for speed boosts). * A [[Crystal extractor]], placed directly next to the helm to be able to use it while manning the helm, during trials. * Crew: [[Cabin Boy Jenkins (ghost)|Cabin Boy Jenkins]], [[Jolly Jim]], [[Jobless Jim]], [[Ex-Captain Siad]]. These four will each be able to carry 2 crates from and to the dock. If a fifth crewmate is available, [[Sailor Jakob]] can optionally man the helm, but otherwise there is no difference between the options for the fifth crew slot. If a helmsman is desired, they should be assigned to either the first or second crew slot to appear on the skiff. In addition to this boat's layout, it is recommended to place a [[Greater teleport focus (facility)|greater teleport focus]] on another boat, to more easily access locations such as [[Sunset Coast]] or [[Lunar Isle]], while doing [[Courier tasks]]. This enables the possibility to park the boat in a location like [[Aldarin]], teleport to the destination port, grab a task from Aldarin to that port, and then teleport back to Aldarin (e.g. using [[Teleport to House]]) to bring cargo there. These so-called 'ABA tasks' obtained in the destination port offer greater experience rewards than tasks that are obtained in the port of the cargo's origin. </tabber>
==Stats== {| class="wikitable" |+ ! Stat !! Explanation |- | Base speed || The fastest speed the boat will go without any boosts. |- | Speed cap || The fastest speed the boat can reach by gaining bursts of speed, ignoring speed gained from wind boosts. Bursts of speed are granted by crossing over rapids, crossing over crystal motes with at least one space open in a wind catcher, breaking ice away from the hull, and entering one of the elven portals on the [[Gwenith Glide]] course.
Each burst of speed gives +0.5 speed. The bursts of speed can be stacked up to the hull's speed cap: for example, the wooden and oak '''raft''' hulls can stack two bursts of speed to gain +1.0 speed, while the rest of the raft hulls will cap at one stack, giving +0.5 speed.{{Fact}}<!-- The preceding about speed caps used to not specify boat types. I'm completely hypothesizing here but it seems very strange & arbitrary to only allow the worst hulls across the board to stack the boosts for more speed.
Looking at the stats (base speed & speed cap) of various hull types, the raft hulls DO follow the rules (now given as an example instead) stated here, but the skiff and sloop ones do not. I'm inclined to assume this was tested early on on rafts only, and that for larger boats the better hulls (up to mahogany for skiffs and ironwood for sloops) can also stack them for increased speed.
I'm not about to verify this myself (sorry about that), but it'd be much appreciated if someone else would, in which case this comment should be removed. --> Whenever a new burst of speed is applied, one stack is gained, up to 5 stacks{{Fact}}, and the boost timer resets to 15 ticks. If these 15 ticks expire, one stack will decay every 4 ticks, until all of the stacks are depleted, removing the boost, or another burst of speed is gained, resetting the timer.
When bursts of speed are combined with wind boosts, boats can reach a speed equal to 0.5 over their listed speed cap. |- | Acceleration || The amount the boat's speed will increase per tick when the double forwards arrow is selected. The speed can only increase up to the boat's base speed, before any bursts of speed or wind boosts are applied.
To get the true acceleration of your boat, divide its Acceleration bonus by 128 and add 0.5. Currently, ships can only have an acceleration of 0.5 or 1.0. |- | Speed boost duration || The time in ticks a wind boost will last for. A wind boost grants +0.5 speed when moving forwards and ignores the boat's speed cap. |- | Armour || For every 100 armour a boat has, it gains one [[flat armour]], decreasing damage from all sources by 1. |- |}

revision.text:
{{Infobox Location |name = Shipwreck Cove |image = [[FIle:Shipwreck Cove.png|300px]] |release = [[25 September]] [[2024]] |update = Varlamore: The Rising Darkness is OUT NOW |members = Yes |location = [[Varlamore]] |music = [[Whispering Wind]] |map = {{Map|name=Shipwreck Cove|width=300|height=250|zoom=2|x=1575|y=3315}} |leagueRegion = Varlamore }} '''Shipwreck Cove''' is a location in northern [[Varlamore]], just west of the [[Salvager Overlook]], and east of the [[Auburn Valley]]. As its name suggests, it is filled with the wrecks of various ships that have washed up on its shores.
==Features== ===Skilling=== There are two fishing spots on the north side of the cove, as well as three more fishing spots on the south-eastern portion of the cove that all offer big net and harpoon fishing. Additionally, there are 3 [[Small shipwreck|small shipwrecks]] and a [[spyglass]] charting location in the vicinity of the cove.
===Spawns=== The cove has multiple spawns of [[seaweed]] scattered around it. There are several [[rope]] and [[plank]] spawns around the cove, as well as single spawns of a [[big fishing net]] and [[small fishing net]] respectively. Two piles of [[bones]] spawn in the general vicinity of the cove.
===Campfire=== [[File:Shipwreck Cove campfire.png|thumb|left|250px|The strange green campfire at the centre of Shipwreck Cove.]] At the centre of the large shipwreck in the middle of the cove, there is a green campfire. Upon inspecting the campfire, the player is met with the message: ''The flames of the campfire burn through strange magic. You find them quite alluring.'' When inspecting the campfire wearing the [[Mask of ranul|Mask of Ranul]] or the [[helmet of the moon]], [[Chosen Aluinus]] will appear and give a message depending on which is worn.
{{Varlamore}}

{{External|rs|rsc}} {{Has calculator|Calculator:Shop calculator}} [[File:Lumbridge General Store stock.png|thumb|400px|The shop stock of a typical store.]] A '''Shop''' is any establishment which allows the trading of [[currencies|currency]] for an item or service, or vice versa. Shop prices may be lower or higher than the equivalent item's price on the [[Grand Exchange]], however, due to their fixed prices, shops cannot be susceptible to the market trends of the Grand Exchange.
==Stock== Each shop has a maximum quantity of items in stock, which differs per item and per shop. Items can only be purchased in batches of 1, 5, 10 and 50. Whenever a shop has less of a certain item than their maximum capacity of that item, the shop will start to restock on that item. The time to restock varies between items. Only a single item will be re-added to the shop per restock, except in the case of [[Ore seller.]] which restocks items in batches. Items that aren't part of the shop's regular stock, or exceed their maximum capacity, will slowly be removed from the shop. Some shops, such as [[Grum's Gold Exchange.]] only have items with 0 stock, and so can only be sold to unless already overstocked from another player selling to them. Ironmen will not be able to purchase anything from these stores as any stocked items will be from other players. As they can only exist at 0 stock or overstocked, their "Restock" timer will only function as a "Destock" timer, and decrement the stock of any items back towards zero. There also exist shops such as [[The Flaming Arrow]] or [[Farming Supplies]] that have infinite stock, and are limited to only allowing the purchase of up to 10 items at a time.
Many shops have separate stock between [[Main account]]s and [[Ironmen]], and stock can be further separated between group, ultimate, and regular ironmen. For example, if an ultimate ironman buys ores from Ore seller, the shop's stock will not decrease for main accounts, group ironmen, or regular ironmen. However, if an ironman sells an item to the [[Pollnivneach general store]], all other account types will see the shop's stock increase.
Any shop that sells a [[Cape of Accomplishment]] has separate stock for players with and without level 99 in the respective skill, and further separate stock for players with that skill as their ''first'' 99, who can purchase an untrimmed cape.
Stock at any given shop always varies between [[worlds]], which some players use to their advantage by [[World switching|hopping worlds]] in order to trade items at the best prices through many small transactions. Multiple shops sometimes share the same stock; for example, buying an item at the [[Void Knight General Store]] decreases that item's stock at [[Jennifer's General Supplies]] in [[Shayzien]].
===Pricing=== Players may sell any tradeable item to a [[general store]] for a fixed [[value]] (usually its low alchemy value), or to specialty shops that specifically stock the item for a fixed higher value (usually its high alchemy value). These values will diminish by a fixed percentage that varies between shops for each stock increase. Regardless of how overstocked they are, all shops will buy the player's items for a minimum of 10% of the item's value. Players may buy any item in stock from a shop for a fixed value. This value will increase by the same fixed percentage mentioned previously for each stock decrease. Specialty shops use their maximum stock quantities as their fixed reference.
For example, a [[steel axe]] has a value of 200 [[coins]]. It can be sold to most general stores for 80 coins (40% of its value), should the shop not have any steel axes in stock. If the player were to sell it to an axe shop such as [[Bob's Brilliant Axes]], then it would sell for 120 coins (60% of its value), should [[Bob]] have his default quantity of 3 steel axes in stock. Since Bob has a fixed percentage change of 2% per sale, then selling a steel axe to him with 4 already in stock would yield 116 coins (58% of its value). If a player were to buy a steel axe from Bob with 3 in stock, it would cost 200 coins. If 4 steel axes were in stock, the price would be 196 coins (98% of its value).

revision.text:
{{External|rs|rsc=Shop_Assistant}} '''Shop assistants''' can be found throughout [[Gielinor]] helping [[shop keeper]]s run [[general store]]s and various specialty shops. Players can still buy and sell [[items]] from the shop assistant for the same prices as the shop keeper would offer. For information about specific shop assistants and their stores' stocks, refer to: *[[Shop assistant (Lumbridge)]] *[[Shop assistant (Varrock)]] *[[Shop assistant (Al Kharid)]] *[[Shop assistant (Falador)]] *[[Shop assistant (Edgeville)]] *[[Shop assistant (Rimmington)]] *[[Shop assistant (Musa Point)]] *[[Shop assistant (Varrock Swordshop)]] *[[Fairy shop assistant]]
==Trivia== * All the shop assistants listed above were originally added in ''[[RuneScape Classic]]'', at a time when due to game engine limitations, only one player could talk to an [[Non-player character|NPC]] at a time. Shops needed assistants so that multiple players could use the shop simultaneously. {{Disambig}}

{{External|rs=Short Green Guy|rsc=SGG}} {{Infobox Item |name = Short green guy |image = [[File:Short green guy.png]] |release = [[12 December]] [[2002]] |update = Agility skill online |aka = SGG |members = Yes |quest = No |tradeable = Yes |equipable = no |stackable = No |noteable = Yes |options = Drink, Drop |examine = A Short Green Guy... looks good. |value = 30 |weight = 0.500 |exchange = Yes |id = 2080 }} [[File:Short green guy detail.png|left|120px]] '''Short green guys''' (commonly abbreviated to '''SGG''') are drinks that can be made at level 20 [[Cooking]], granting 120 Cooking [[experience]]. They heal 5 [[hitpoints]], boost [[Strength]] by 5% + 1 levels, and reduce [[Attack]] by 2% - 3 levels. Short green guys are a good way to cheaply train without leaving the [[Gnome Stronghold]], since they require only one type of fruit, have cheap ingredients, and only require one chopped/sliced item. ==Effects== ===Strength boost=== Temporarily increases [[Strength]] by \lfloor StrengthLevel \times \frac{5}{100} \rfloor + 1 {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center" !{{SCP|Strength}} Level!!Boost |- |'''1-19'''||1 |- |'''20-39'''||2 |- |'''40-59'''||3 |- |'''60-79'''||4 |- |'''80-99'''||5 |} ===Attack drain=== Temporarily reduces [[Attack]] by \lfloor AttackLevel \times \frac{2}{100} \rfloor + 3 {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center" !{{SCP|Attack}} Level!!Boost |- |'''1-49'''||-3 |- |'''50-99'''||-4 |} ==Ingredients== {|class="wikitable" |Short Green Guy [[File:Short green guy.png]] |[[File:Vodka.png]] 1 [[Vodka]], [[File:Lime.png]][[File:Lime.png]][[File:Lime.png]] 3 [[lime]]s |1 sliced [[lime]] [[File:Lime slices.png]], 1 [[Equa leaves|Equa leaf]] [[File:Equa leaves.png]] |} ==Creation== {{Recipe |skill1 = Cooking |skill1lvl = 20 |skill1boostable = Yes |skill1exp = 90 |members = Yes |ticks = 0 |mat1 = Mixed sgg |mat1cost = No |mat2 = Lime slices |mat3 = Equa leaves |mat4 = Cocktail glass |output1 = Short green guy }} ==Item sources== {{Drop sources|Short green guy}} ===Shop locations=== {{Store locations list|Short green guy}} ==Changes== {{Subject changes header}} {{Subject changes |date = 7 August 2006 |update = Gnome Cuisine |change = The item was graphically updated with the rework of the [[Gnome Restaurant]]. }} {{Subject changes |daterange = 26 April –
6 June 2005 |change = The item was renamed from "Sgg" to "Short green guy". }} {{Subject changes footer}} ===Gallery (historical)=== {|style="text-align: center" cellpadding="15" |[[File:Short green guy detail (beta).png|center|300x150px]] |[[File:Short green guy detail (historical).png|center|300x150px]] |[[File:Short green guy detail.png|center|300x150px]] |- |[[File:Short green guy (beta).png|center]] |[[File:Short green guy (historical).png|center]] |[[File:Short green guy.png|center]] |- |RuneScape 2

present |} ==Trivia== *This might be a reference to a popular rule in drinking games, the "Little Green Man Rule," where people drinking must remove an invisible green man from their glasses before taking a drink. *The name is also a reference to [[gnome]]s since they are short guys, and in ''[[RuneScape Classic]]'' had green skin. {{Gnome cooking}} {{Alcoholic beverages}} [[Category:Temporary skill boost]] [[Category:Strength boosting items]]

{{External|rs|rsc}} {{otheruses|def=no|shortbows in general|Shortbow (weapon)}} {{Infobox Item |name = Shortbow |image = [[File:Shortbow.png]] |release = [[4 January]] [[2001]] |update = Runescape beta is now online! |members = No |quest = No |tradeable = Yes |equipable = Yes |stackable = No |noteable = Yes |options = Wield, Drop |examine = Short but effective. |value = 50 |weight = 1.360 |respawn = 200 |exchange = Yes |id = 841 }} [[File:Shortbow detail.png|left|100px]] The '''shortbow''' is the weakest [[Shortbow (weapon)|bow]] in ''[[Old School RuneScape]]'' and can use arrows up to [[iron arrows|iron]]. Players can purchase this bow from [[Lowe's Archery Emporium]] in [[Varrock]]. Players are supplied with this bow along with several [[bronze arrows]] as their first [[ranged weapon]] on [[Tutorial Island]]. [[Members]] can make a shortbow through the [[Fletching]] skill at level 5. First, a player must cut an [[Shortbow (u)|unstrung shortbow]] from [[logs]], granting 5 Fletching [[experience]]. Then, the player must string the [[Shortbow (u)|unstrung shortbow]] with a [[bow string]], granting 5 experience. ==Combat stats== {{Infobox Bonuses |astab = 0 |aslash = 0 |acrush = 0 |amagic = 0 |arange = +8 |dstab = 0 |dslash = 0 |dcrush = 0 |dmagic = 0 |drange = 0 |str = 0 |rstr = 0 |mdmg = 0 |prayer = 0 |slot = 2h |speed = 4 |attackrange = 7 |combatstyle = Bow |image = [[File:Shortbow equipped.png]] |altimage = [[File:Shortbow equipped female.png]] }} {{CombatStyles|Bow|speed=4|attackrange=7}} ==Creation== {{Recipe |skill1 = Fletching |skill1lvl = 5 |skill1boostable = Yes |skill1exp = 5 |members = Yes |ticks = 2 |mat1 = Shortbow (u) |mat2 = Bow string |output1 = Shortbow }} ==Item sources== {{Drop sources|Shortbow}} ===Shop locations=== {{Store locations list|Shortbow}} ===Item spawns=== {{ItemSpawnTableHead}} {{ItemSpawnLine|name=Shortbow|location=[[Kharidian Desert]] - north-west of the [[Uzer Hunter area]]|members=Yes|3389,3123|leagueRegion=desert}} {{ItemSpawnLine|name=Shortbow|location=[[Taverley]] - building directly west of the tree patch ({{FloorNumber|uk=1}})|members=Yes|plane=1 |2914,3439|leagueRegion=asgarnia}} {{ItemSpawnTableBottom}} ==Changes== {{Subject changes header}} {{Subject changes |date = 26 January 2005 |update = Slayer Skill |change = The item was graphically updated. }} {{Subject changes |daterange = 1 – 28 June 2004 |change = The item was recoloured. }} {{Subject changes footer}} ===Gallery (historical)=== {|style="text-align: center" cellpadding="15" |[[File:Shortbow detail (historical, v1).png|center|300x150px]] |[[File:Shortbow detail (historical, v2).png|center|300x150px]] |[[File:Shortbow detail.png|center|300x150px]] |- |[[File:Shortbow (historical, v1).png|center]] |[[File:Shortbow (historical, v2).png|center]] |[[File:Shortbow.png|center]] |- |29 March 2004 –

{{External|rs}} {{Confuse|Shortcut keys}}{{Gone|update=A Taste of Hope}} {{Infobox Item |name = Shortcut key |image = [[File:Shortcut key.png]] |release = [[4 September]] [[2006]] |update = Myreque Pt III - Darkness of Hallowvale |removal = [[24 May]] [[2018]] |removalupdate = A Taste of Hope |members = Yes |quest = [[Darkness of Hallowvale]] |tradeable = No |equipable = No |stackable = No |noteable = |options = Destroy |destroy = Safalaan gave you this key as a reward for helping out in Meiyerditch, you can get another key from him. |examine = A key allowing a shortcut into the Sanguinesti region (Quick access through Meiyerditch). |value = 1 |weight = 0.055 |id = hist9662 }} [[File:Shortcut key detail.png|left|120px]] The '''shortcut key''' was obtained near the end of the [[Darkness of Hallowvale]] quest. With the shortcut key, the time to reach sector 3 from the start is cut to around a third. There are two shortcut doors which are identified by the symbol of the key on them. The shortcut key could be placed on the [[steel key ring]]. If you lost your shortcut key you could get another from [[Safalaan]]. Note that if the key was on your steel key ring when you lost it, then you could not get another key from Safalaan until you reclaim the ring. The shortcut key was removed after {{UD|A Taste of Hope|an update}} on [[24 May]] [[2018]]{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Wolf|url=https://twitter.com/JagexWolf/status/999607060257017856|date=24 May 2018|archiveurl=https://archive.is/Sm4Za|archivedate=30 May 2020|quote=Those assisting the Myreque today may notice they no longer have their shortcut key. This is no longer an item given after the Darkness of Hallowvale quest and you may now simply use the shortcut doors after the quest without a key.}}. However, those who did not have the key, but kept its [[bank]] placeholder had the key replaced with a [[useless key]]. ==Changes== {{Subject changes header}} {{Subject changes |date = 10 December 2015 |update = Key Update & Seaweed |poll = Old School Content Poll 37: Skillcape Perks |change = The examine of this key has been updated from "''A key allowing a shortcut into the Sanguinesti region.''" to "''A key allowing a shortcut into the Sanguinesti region (Quick access through Meiyerditch).''" so its purpose is better described. }} {{Subject changes footer}} ===Gallery (historical)=== {|style="text-align: center" cellpadding="15" |[[File:Shortcut key (v1) detail.png|center|300x150px]] |[[File:Shortcut key detail.png|center|300x150px]] |- |[[File:Shortcut key v1.png|center]] |[[File:Shortcut key.png|center]] |- |4 September 2006 –

{{External|rs}} {{otheruses|Agility shortcuts|the passageway discovered midway during ''[[In Search of the Myreque]]'' between [[Canifis]] and the [[Hollows]]|Myreque Shortcut}} '''Shortcuts''' can be found all around [[Gielinor]]. By climbing cliff sides, crossing rivers and squeezing through crevices, it is possible to reach a destination more directly than by the alternative route. Nearly all shortcuts require the proper [[Agility]] level. There are no guaranteed rewards for using shortcuts, except that they will save you time, but they will sometimes give small amounts of Agility experience. All shortcuts, Asgarnian Ice Dungeon [[Tunnel (Asgarnian Ice Dungeon, level 60)|tunnel]], and crandor south [[Rocks (Crandor)|rocks]], are [[P2P]], and some require [[Ranged]] and [[Strength]] levels. Two-way shortcuts are identified with a twisting green arrow icon ([[File:Agility shortcut icon.png]]) on the [[minimap]], with one-way shortcuts using an inverted arrow icon ([[File:Agility shortcut (One way) icon.png]]). Agility '''Areas''' are locations that are locked behind an obstacle with an Agility requirement. There is no standard way to access these locations, although some such as the [[God Wars Dungeon]] have an alternative entrance using a different skill. ==List of shortcuts== This is a list of all Agility shortcuts. {{clear}} {| class="wikitable sortable align-center-1 align-center-2 align-center-6 sticky-header" !Level(s) !Icon !Shortcut ! class="unsortable" |Location ! class="unsortable" |Notes !XP |- |{{SCP|Agility|1}} |[[File:Agility shortcut jump.png]] |[[Stepping stone (Lumbridge Swamp Caves)|Stepping stones]] |[[Lumbridge Swamp Caves]] stepping stones |Stepping stones in the central Lumbridge Swamp Caves. This shortcut provides varying experience for success and failure. |3 (1 on failure) |- |{{SCP|Agility|5}} |[[File:Agility shortcut climb.png]] |[[Crumbling wall (Falador)|Crumbling wall]] |[[Falador]] [[Agility]] Shortcut |Right next to the [[Falador west bank]]. Provides easy access to the areas south of [[Taverley]]. |0.5 |- |{{SCP|Agility|5}} |{{NA}} |[[Climbing rocks (Yanille)|Climbing rocks]] |[[Yanille]] |Not labelled on the map. revision.text:
'''Shrine''' may refer to:
* [[Shrines]], sacred constructions made to honor or worship a person or thing * [[Shrine]], a shrine found in the [[Woodcutting Guild]] that can be offered [[Bird's egg|bird's eggs]] * [[Vending shrine]], a former [[Last Man Standing]] item for using [[Survival token|survival tokens]] {{Disambig}}

{{Cache}} {{Infobox Item |name = Shrine |image = [[File:Pink skirt.png]] |release = April-June [[2005]] |update = |removal = [[23 October]] [[2006]] |removalupdate = Would you like to see My Arm? |members = No |quest = No |tradeable = No |equipable = No |stackable = No |noteable = No |options = Drop |examine = Sanctity in your pocket. |value = 1 |weight = |id = hist4001 }} [[File:Pink skirt detail.png|left|120px]] '''Shrine''' was an unobtainable item that previously could be found in the game cache. It was created to replace the noted form of [[Iodine]]. Since items could not be fully removed once created, it was added in a hidden update in 2005 to fill this slot.
The name and examine were designed to be inconspicuous, but the actual item was just a copy of a pink skirt. Originally, players had the option to "Activate" it. If players attempted to view the Shrine in game by using cheating software, they would be given a [[Hex edit detected]] instead.
In ''RuneScape'', the item later became viewable via Quick Chat, causing much confusion.
It was deleted from the game cache in 2006, being replaced by the [[Hardy gout tuber]] from [[My Arm's Big Adventure]].
==Changes== {{Subject changes header}} {{Subject changes |daterange = 11 – 19 July 2005 |change = The "Activate" option was replaced with a fake "Wear" option. }} {{Subject changes footer}}

{{External|rs}} {{Infobox Item |name = Shrink-me-quick |image = [[File:Shrink-me-quick.png]] |release = [[4 June]] [[2007]] |update = Grim Tales |members = Yes |quest = [[Grim Tales]] |tradeable = No |equipable = No |stackable = No |noteable = No |options = Drink, Empty, Destroy |destroy = You will need to make another shrinking potion if you destroy this. |examine = Apparently it shrinks you. Very fast. |value = 1 |weight = 0.035 |id = 11204 }} [[File:Shrink-me-quick detail.png|left|100px]] The '''shrink-me-quick''' is a [[quest items|quest item]] used during the [[Grim Tales]] [[quests|quest]]. It is created by adding a [[tarromin]] to a [[vial of water]], and then adding a [[shrunk ogleroot]]. The potion can then be drunk by the player in order to go through a [[Mouse hole|mouse hole]] in the witch's house in [[Taverley]] in order to recover [[Miazrqa's pendant]] from a mouse that stole it. The potion can still be made and used after completion of the quest.
The potion is made through the [[Herblore]] skill, and requires a level of 52, and gives 6 experience when made. Players may use boosts such as [[Greenman's ale|Greenman's Ale]].
==Creation== {{Recipe |skill1 = Herblore |skill1lvl = 52 |skill1boostable = Yes |skill1exp = 6 |members = Yes |ticks = 0 |mat1 = Tarromin potion (unf) |mat2 = Shrunk ogleroot |output1 = Shrink-me-quick |output1cost = No }}
==Barbarian Assault== [[File:Shrink-me-quick Barbarian Assault drink.webp|right|thumb|width=150px|The unique animation played within Barbarian Assault.]]
Attempting to drink the shrink-me-quick potion in [[Barbarian Assault]] will not consume the potion, but will instead play a unique animation. Because actions and [[egg hopper]] count in Barbarian Assault is directly tied to the party leader, usage of shrink-me-quick is a common exploit to extend durations between calls and when fighting the [[Penance Queen]]. A party leader using shrink-me-quick while the egg hopper is being fired at the Queen will prevent the eggs from running out, allowing teams to kill her with only a single egg if timed correctly.
==Trivia== *Shrink-me-quick is a reference to "drink-me-quick", the label on a bottle of liquid that Alice drank in Lewis Carroll's ''[[wikipedia:Alice's Adventures in Wonderland|Alice's Adventures in Wonderland]]'' that allows Alice to go into a very strange hole that takes her to [[wikipedia:Wonderland (fictional country)|Wonderland]]. *When a player tries to drink a shrink-me-quick potion outside the room with the mouse hole, the potion will not be consumed, but will instead give the message "It smells absolutely vile. You don't want to drink it unless you're somewhere you can make use of it."
*Attempting to drink the shrink-me-quick potion in front of the mouse hole whilst the player has a pet cat following them will result in the message "Being mouse-sized with a cat around may not be such a good idea..." *The colour of the shrunk ogleroot inside the vial changes according to the player's default skin tone, and can therefore be changed by visiting a [[makeover]] service. The variants are shown below: <gallery> Shrink-me-quick (skin tone 7, very pale) equipped male.png|Very pale Shrink-me-quick (skin tone 0, pale) equipped male.png|Pale Shrink-me-quick (skin tone 1, light) equipped male.png|Light Shrink-me-quick (skin tone 2, slightly tan) equipped male.png|Slightly tan Shrink-me-quick (skin tone 3, tan) equipped male.png|Tan Shrink-me-quick (skin tone 4, very tan) equipped male.png|Very tan Shrink-me-quick (skin tone 5, dark) equipped male.png|Dark Shrink-me-quick (skin tone 6, very dark) equipped male.png|Very dark Shrink-me-quick (skin tone 8, green) equipped male.png|Green Shrink-me-quick (skin tone 9, black) equipped male.png|Black Shrink-me-quick (skin tone 10, white) equipped male.png|White Shrink-me-quick (skin tone 11, cyan) equipped male.png|Cyan Shrink-me-quick (skin tone 12, purple) equipped male.png|Purple </gallery>

revision.text:
{{External|rs|rsc=Plague sheep}} The '''Sick-looking sheep''' are a collection of sixteen [[sheep]] that are coloured. They are [[Non-player character|NPCs]] involved in the [[Sheep Herder]] and [[Mourning's End Part I]] [[quests]]. The sheep are supposedly infected with the plague and must be incinerated, but later it is revealed that they've simply been dyed.
*[[Red Sheep]] are tinted red and located near the [[East Ardougne]] north bank. *[[Green Sheep]] are tinted green and located north of East Ardougne near a potato field. *[[Blue Sheep]] are tinted blue and located near the river south of [[Baxtorian Falls]]. *[[Yellow Sheep]] are tinted yellow and located near the [[Fishing Guild]].
{{Sheep Herder}} [[Category:Quest NPCs]]

{{External|rs}} {{Infobox Item |name = Sickle mould |image = [[File:Sickle mould.png]] |release = [[13 July]] [[2004]] |update = Nature Spirit Quest |members = Yes |quest = No |tradeable = Yes |equipable = No |stackable = No |noteable = Yes |options = Drop |examine = Used to make sickles. |value = 10 |weight = 0.453 |exchange = Yes |id = 2976 }} [[File:Sickle mould detail.png|left|130px]] A '''sickle mould''' is a type of mould that can be used together with a [[silver bar]] to create a [[silver sickle]]. One can make a silver sickle at a [[Crafting]] level of 18. The sickle mould can be purchased from the following [[shop]]s: *[[Dommik's Crafting Store.|Dommik's Crafting Store]] in [[Al Kharid]] *[[Jamila's Craft Stall]] in [[Sophanem]] *[[Rasolo the Wandering Merchant]] west of the [[Fishing Guild]] *[[Rommik's Crafty Supplies]] in [[Rimmington]] ==Products== {{Uses tool list|Sickle mould}} ==Shop locations== {{Store locations list|Sickle mould}} ==Changes== {{Subject changes header}} {{Subject changes |daterange = 26 April –
6 June 2005 |change = The item's examine was changed from "''Used to make sickles''"{{sic}} to "''Used to make sickles.''" }} {{Subject changes footer}} {{Nature Spirit}} {{Mould}} [[Category:Moulds]]

Like all sigils, the un-attuned version is dropped by most monsters (via the [[Drop table#Deadman Mode|Deadman Mode drop table]]) and is tradeable on the [[Grand Exchange]]. It can be activated by clicking ''Attune''. ==Effect== {|class=wikitable !Event !Effect |- |[[Deadman: Armageddon]] |Activate the Sigil to get a 75% magic accuracy buff on your next binding spell within the next 12 seconds. The Sigil has a 15 second cooldown. |- |[[Deadman: Apocalypse]] |Activate the Sigil to get a 75% magic accuracy buff on your next binding spell within the next 12 seconds. The Sigil has a 30 second cooldown. |- |[[Deadman: Reborn]] |Activate the Sigil to get a 75% magic accuracy buff on your next binding spell within the next 12 seconds. If the bind was successful, the Sigil has a 5-minute cooldown. {{Deadman seasonal}} {{Infobox Item |version1 = Un-attuned |version2 = Attuned |name = Sigil of enhanced harvest |image1 = [[File:Sigil of enhanced harvest.png]] |image2 = [[File:Sigil of enhanced harvest (attuned).png]] |release = [[25 August]] [[2021]] |update = Deadman: Reborn |members = Yes |quest = No |tradeable1 = No |tradeable2 = No |equipable = No |stackable = No |noteable = No |options1 = Unlock, Inspect, Destroy |options2 = Destroy |destroy1 = You can sell duplicate sigils by using them on Deadman's skull. |destroy2 = You must unattune the Sigil before you can destroy it. |examine1 = You always gain triple resources from Mining, Fishing, Woodcutting or Farming. Does not work at Tithe Farm. |examine2 = A sigil attuned to you with great power. |value = 1 |weight = 0.100 |id1 = 26018 |id2 = 26017 }} {{Synced switch |version1 = [[File:Sigil of enhanced harvest detail.png|left|150px]] |version2 = [[File:Sigil of enhanced harvest (attuned) detail.png|left|150px]] }} The '''Sigil of Enhanced Harvest''' is a tier 1 skilling [[Deadman Mode]] [[sigil]]. It is a toggleable permanent unlock that yields triple resources from [[Mining]], [[Fishing]], [[Woodcutting]], and [[Farming]]. It is a toggleable unlock and can be toggled on and off through the "Unlocks" option on the [[deadman's skull]]. In [[Deadman: Annihilation]], it can be purchased from the [[Deadman: Annihilation/Skull shop|skull shop]]. It can be activated by clicking ''Attune'' and is a permanent unlock. There is no limit on how many permanent sigils can be active at once. Duplicate sigils can be sold back to the skull shop by using it on the [[deadman's skull]]. In past [[Deadman Mode]] events, the un-attuned version was dropped by most monsters (via the [[Drop table#Deadman Mode|Deadman Mode drop table]]) and was tradeable on the [[Grand Exchange]]. This sigil '''does not''' work at [[Tithe Farm]]. ==Effect== {|class=wikitable !Event !Effect |- class="table-yes" |[[Deadman: Annihilation]] |You always gain triple resources from Mining, Fishing, Woodcutting or Farming. Does not work at Tithe Farm. |- |[[Deadman: Armageddon]] |You always gain triple resources from Mining, Fishing, Woodcutting or Farming. This sigil does not stack with [[Sigil of the Forager]]. |- |[[Deadman: Apocalypse]] |You always gain quintuple resources from Mining, Fishing, Woodcutting or Farming. This sigil does not stack with [[Sigil of the Forager]]. |- |[[Deadman: Reborn]] |You have a 50% chance to gain double resources from Mining, Fishing, Woodcutting or Farming. Does not stack with Sigil of the forager. |} ==Changes== {{Subject changes header}} {{Subject changes |date = 23 August 2023 |update = Deadman: Apocalypse - Friday 25th August |change = * The sigil now has a different effect for Deadman: Apocalypse. * The item has been [[graphically updated]]. }} {{Subject changes footer}} ===Gallery (historical)=== {{Switch infobox |text1 = Un-attuned |item1 = |text2 = Attuned |item2 = }} {|style="text-align: center" cellpadding="15" | {{Synced switch |version1 = [[File:Sigil of enhanced harvest v1 detail.png|center|300x150px]] |version2 = [[File:Sigil of enhanced harvest (attuned) v1 detail.png|center|300x150px]] }} | {{Synced switch |version1 = [[File:Sigil of enhanced harvest detail.png|center|300x150px]] |version2 = [[File:Sigil of enhanced harvest (attuned) detail.png|center|300x150px]] }} |- | {{Synced switch |version1 = [[File:Sigil of enhanced harvest v1.png|center]] |version2 = [[File:Sigil of enhanced harvest (attuned) v1.png|center]] }} | {{Synced switch |version1 = [[File:Sigil of enhanced harvest.png|center]] |version2 = [[File:Sigil of enhanced harvest (attuned).png|center]] }} |- |25 August 2021 –

{{Deadman seasonal}} {{Infobox Item |version1 = Un-attuned |version2 = Attuned |name = Sigil of escaping |image1 = [[File:Sigil of escaping.png]] |image2 = [[File:Sigil of escaping (attuned).png]] |release = [[25 August]] [[2021]] |update = Deadman: Reborn |members = Yes |quest = No |tradeable1 = No |tradeable2 = No |equipable = No |stackable = No |noteable = No |options1 = Attune, Inspect, Destroy |options2 = Activate, Check, Inspect, Unattune, Destroy |destroy1 = An alternative is to sell it on the Grand Exchange. |destroy2 = You must unattune the Sigil before you can destroy it. |examine1 = A power enhancing sigil not yet attuned to you. |examine2 = A sigil attuned to you with great power. |value = 1 |weight = 0.100 |exchange1 = Yes |exchange2 = No |id1 = 26069 |id2 = 26068 }} {{Synced switch |version1 = [[File:Sigil of escaping detail.png|left|150px]] |version2 = [[File:Sigil of escaping (attuned) detail.png|left|150px]] }} The '''Sigil of Escaping''' is a tier 2 combat sigil in [[Deadman: Reborn]]. Like all sigils, the un-attuned version is dropped by most monsters (via the [[Drop table#Deadman Mode|Deadman Mode drop table]]) and is tradeable on the [[Grand Exchange]]. It can be activated by clicking ''Attune''.
While attuned, the sigil gives you the following property:
''Activate the Sigil to get a 75% increased chance to resist the first bind effect that is cast on you within the next 12 seconds. If the bind was not successful, the Sigil has a 5-minute cooldown. If it successfully binds you, the Sigil has a 1-minute cooldown.''
[[File:Sigil of escaping.gif|thumb|left|200px|The Sigil of escaping when activated.]]
{{Deadman: Reborn}}

{{Deadman seasonal}} {{Infobox Item |version1 = Un-attuned |version2 = Attuned |name = Sigil of finality |image1 = [[File:Sigil of finality.png]] |image2 = [[File:Sigil of finality (attuned).png]] |release = [[25 August]] [[2021]] |update = Deadman: Reborn |members = Yes |quest = No |tradeable1 = No |tradeable2 = No |equipable = No |stackable = No |noteable = No |options1 = Attune, Inspect, Destroy |options2 = Activate, Check, Inspect, Unattune, Destroy |destroy1 = You can sell duplicate sigils by using them on Deadman's skull. |destroy2 = You must unattune the Sigil before you can destroy it. |examine1 = Activate the sigil to guarantee 100% accuracy on your next special attack within the next 12 seconds. It is an attunable sigil that, when activated, guarantees 100% accuracy on your next [[special attack]]. It must be carried in the [[inventory]] to be used. In [[Deadman: Annihilation]], the un-attuned version can be purchased from the [[Deadman: Annihilation/Skull shop|skull shop]]. It can be activated by clicking ''Attune''. Up to three attunable sigils can be attuned at once. Duplicate sigils can be sold back to the skull shop by using them on the [[deadman's skull]]. In past [[Deadman Mode]] events, the un-attuned version was dropped by most monsters (via the [[Drop table#Deadman Mode|Deadman Mode drop table]]) and was tradeable on the [[Grand Exchange]]. ==Effect== {|class=wikitable !Event !Effect |- class="table-yes" |[[Deadman: Annihilation]] |Activate the sigil to guarantee 100% accuracy on your next [[special attack]] within the next 12 seconds. Once activated, the sigil has a 10 second cooldown. |- |[[Deadman: Armageddon]] |Activate the Sigil to guarantee 100% accuracy on your next special attack within the next 12 seconds. Once activated, the Sigil has a 30 second cooldown. |- |[[Deadman: Apocalypse]] |Activate the Sigil to guarantee 100% accuracy on your next special attack within the next 12 seconds. Once activated, the Sigil has a 1-minute cooldown. |- |[[Deadman: Reborn]] |Activate the Sigil to guarantee 100% accuracy on your next special attack. Once activated, the Sigil has a 2-minute cooldown. |} ==Changes== {{Subject changes header}} {{Subject changes |date = 23 August 2023 |update = Deadman: Apocalypse - Friday 25th August |change = * The sigil now has a different effect for Deadman: Apocalypse. * The item has been [[graphically updated]]. }} {{Subject changes footer}} ===Gallery (historical)=== {{Switch infobox |text1 = Un-attuned |item1 = |text2 = Attuned |item2 = }} {|style="text-align: center" cellpadding="15" | {{Synced switch |version1 = [[File:Sigil of finality v1 detail.png|center|300x150px]] |version2 = [[File:Sigil of finality (attuned) v1 detail.png|center|300x150px]] }} | {{Synced switch |version1 = [[File:Sigil of finality detail.png|center|300x150px]] |version2 = [[File:Sigil of finality (attuned) detail.png|center|300x150px]] }} |- | {{Synced switch |version1 = [[File:Sigil of finality v1.png|center]] |version2 = [[File:Sigil of finality (attuned) v1.png|center]] }} | {{Synced switch |version1 = [[File:Sigil of finality.png|center]] |version2 = [[File:Sigil of finality (attuned).png|center]] }} |- |25 August 2021 –

{{Deadman seasonal}} {{Infobox Item |version1 = Un-attuned |version2 = Attuned |name = Sigil of slaughter |image1 = [[File:Sigil of slaughter.png]] |image2 = [[File:Sigil of slaughter (attuned).png]] |release = [[25 August]] [[2021]] |update = Deadman: Reborn |members = Yes |quest = No |tradeable1 = No |tradeable2 = No |equipable = No |stackable = No |noteable = No |options1 = Unlock, Inspect, Destroy |options2 = Destroy |destroy1 = You can sell duplicate sigils by using them on Deadman's skull. |destroy2 = You must unattune the Sigil before you can destroy it. |examine1 = Pay 45 Slayer Points to choose your own non-boss specific Slayer Task. Double the chance of a superior slayer monster appearing. Toggled on, you have a 25% chance for a Slayer Task kill to not count towards the task while still gaining you Slayer XP. Toggled off, 25% chance for a kill to count as 2. This Sigil does not stack with any bracelet effects. |examine2 = A sigil attuned to you with great power. |value = 1 |weight = 0.100 |id1 = 26108 |id2 = 26107 }} {{Synced switch |version1 = [[File:Sigil of slaughter detail.png|left|150px]] |version2 = [[File:Sigil of slaughter (attuned) detail.png|left|150px]] }} The '''Sigil of Slaughter''' is a tier 2 utility [[Deadman Mode]] sigil. It is a permanent unlock and allows you to pay [[Slayer points]] to choose a [[Slayer task]] (bosses not included). It also doubles the chance of a [[superior slayer monster]] appearing. It also has a toggleable effect: when toggled on, it gives a 25% chance for a kill to not count towards the current task; when toggled off, it gives a 25% chance for a kill to count as double towards the current task. This effect does not stack with any [[Slayer bracelets|Slayer bracelet]] effects. In order to pick a task, you must have no active task. The next time you go to get a slayer task, you will have the option of spending points to choose the task you want. It is a toggleable unlock and can be toggled on and off through the "Unlocks" option on the [[deadman's skull]]. In [[Deadman: Annihilation]], it can be purchased from the [[Deadman: Annihilation/Skull shop|skull shop]]. It can be activated by clicking ''Attune'' and is a permanent unlock. There is no limit on how many permanent sigils can be active at once. Duplicate sigils can be sold back to the skull shop by using them on the [[deadman's skull]]. In past [[Deadman Mode]] events, the un-attuned version was dropped by most monsters (via the [[Drop table#Deadman Mode|Deadman Mode drop table]]) and was tradeable on the [[Grand Exchange]]. ==Effect== {|class=wikitable !Event !Effect |- class="table-yes" |[[Deadman: Annihilation]] |Pay 45 [[Slayer points|Slayer Points]] to choose your own non-boss specific [[Slayer task|Slayer Task]]. Double the chance of a [[superior slayer monster]] appearing. Toggled on, you have a 25% chance for a Slayer Task kill to not count towards the task while still gaining you Slayer XP. Toggled off, 25% chance for a kill to count as 2. This Sigil does not stack with any [[Slayer bracelets|bracelet effects]]. |- |[[Deadman: Armageddon]] |Pay 60 Slayer Points to choose your own Slayer Task. You have a 50% chance for a Slayer Task kill to not count towards the task while still gaining you Slayer XP. This Sigil does not stack with any bracelet effects. |- |[[Deadman: Apocalypse]] |Pay 30 Slayer Points to choose your own Slayer Task. You have a 50% chance for a Slayer Task kill to not count towards the task while still gaining you Slayer XP. This Sigil does not stack with any bracelet effects. |- |[[Deadman: Reborn]] |Pay 30 Slayer Points to choose your own Slayer Task. You have a 25% chance for a Slayer Task kill to not count towards the task while still gaining you Slayer XP. This Sigil does not stack with any bracelet effects. |} ==Changes== {{Subject changes header}} {{Subject changes |date = 24 July 2024 |update = Deadman: Armageddon & While Guthix Sleeps Tweaks |change = The number of [[Slayer points]] required to choose a [[Slayer task|task]] when using the Sigil of Slaughter has been increased from 30 to 60. }} {{Subject changes |date = 23 August 2023 |update = Deadman: Apocalypse - Friday 25th August |change = * The sigil now has a different effect for Deadman: Apocalypse. * The item has been [[graphically updated]]. }} {{Subject changes footer}} ===Gallery (historical)=== {{Switch infobox |text1 = Un-attuned |item1 = |text2 = Attuned |item2 = }} {|style="text-align: center" cellpadding="15" | {{Synced switch |version1 = [[File:Sigil of slaughter v1 detail.png|center|300x150px]] |version2 = [[File:Sigil of slaughter (attuned) v1 detail.png|center|300x150px]] }} | {{Synced switch |version1 = [[File:Sigil of slaughter detail.png|center|300x150px]] |version2 = [[File:Sigil of slaughter (attuned) detail.png|center|300x150px]] }} |- | {{Synced switch |version1 = [[File:Sigil of slaughter v1.png|center]] |version2 = [[File:Sigil of slaughter (attuned) v1.png|center]] }} | {{Synced switch |version1 = [[File:Sigil of slaughter.png|center]] |version2 = [[File:Sigil of slaughter (attuned).png|center]] }} |- |25 August 2021 –

|members = Yes |combat = 50 |size = 1 |examine = Former advisor to the Duke of Lumbridge. |xpbonus = 0 |max hit = 5 |aggressive = Yes |poisonous = No |attack style = [[Crush]] |attack speed = 4 |hitpoints = 60 |att = 45 |str = 45 |def = 24 |mage = 1 |range = 1 |attbns = 0 |strbns = 0 |amagic = 8 |mbns = 0 |arange = 0 |rngbns = 0 |dstab = 0 |dslash = 0 |dcrush = 0 |dmagic = 0 |dlight = 0 |dstandard = 0 |dheavy = 0 |poisonresistance = 0 |venomresistance = 100 |id = 990,991,992,993,994,4328 |leagueRegion = Misthalin }} [[File:Sigmund (H.A.M.) chathead.png|left]] |text4 = Another Slice of H.A.M. |item4 = {{Infobox Monster |bucketname = Another Slice of H.A.M. |name = Sigmund |image = [[File:Sigmund (monster).png|150px]] |release = [[24 April]] [[2007]] |update = Another Slice of H.A.M. |members = Yes |combat = 64 |size = 1 |examine = Former advisor to the Duke of Lumbridge. |xpbonus = 0 |max hit = 6 |aggressive = Yes |poisonous = No |attack style = [[Crush]] |attack speed = 4 |hitpoints = 70 |att = 55 |str = 55 |def = 44 |mage = 1 |range = 1 |attbns = 0 |strbns = 0 |amagic = 8 |mbns = 0 |arange = 0 |rngbns = 0 |dstab = 0 |dslash = 0 |dcrush = 0 |dmagic = 0 |dlight = 0 |dstandard = 0 |dheavy = 0 |poisonresistance = 0 |venomresistance = 0 |id = 5139,5142,5143,5144,5145,5146,5329 |leagueRegion = Misthalin }} [[File:Sigmund (H.A.M.) chathead.png|left]] }} '''Sigmund''' is a high-ranking member of [[Humans Against Monsters]], a former advisor to [[Duke Horacio]] and the main antagonist in the [[List of quest series#Dorgeshuun series|Dorgeshuun quest series]]. He has been involved in three attempts to destroy the [[Dorgeshuun]] [[goblin (race)|goblins]]. The first was during [[The Lost Tribe]] [[quest]], the second during the [[Death to the Dorgeshuun]] quest, and again in the [[Another Slice of H.A.M.]] quest. ==The Lost Tribe== During this quest, the player is sent to recover silverware allegedly stolen by underground goblins. During this quest, it is discovered that Sigmund has taken the silverware and is a member of [[Humans Against Monsters]]. His attempts at creating a war between [[Misthalin]] and the [[Dorgeshuun]] were thwarted, and he was dismissed for treason by [[Duke Horacio]]. ==Death to the Dorgeshuun== During the [[Death to the Dorgeshuun]] quest, it is revealed by a [[Humans Against Monsters|H.A.M]] member that Sigmund and [[Johanhus Ulsbrecht]], head of H.A.M, are 'planning something big'. After eavesdropping on the H.A.M council, it is discovered that they are using a machine they bought from the dwarves of [[Keldagrim]] for unknown purposes. Once the dead Dorgeshuun [[Zanik]] has been revived, she reveals that the H.A.M are going to use the machine to flood the [[Dorgeshuun]] capital, [[Dorgesh-Kaan]]. After infiltrating the [[water mill cellar]] with the machine in it and slaying the H.A.M helpers, the player and Zanik battle the level 50 Sigmund. Using a [[ring of life]], he escapes death and swears that they will meet again. The ring works even if you reduce his [[Hitpoints]] to 0. During this battle, the player discovers Sigmund is a [[Saradomin]]ist; he uses a [[protection prayer]] called up by the powers of Saradomin. ===Combat Strategy=== Sigmund is rather simple to defeat. First, players must defeat his cronies. Afterwards, both the player and [[Zanik]] can focus on Sigmund alone. Sigmund, probably out of spite of Zanik, will use [[Protect from Missiles]] rather than the [[protection prayer]] against whatever [[combat style]] you use, thus making him vulnerable. If Sigmund proves to be too much of a threat to the player, it is also possible to safespot him using the crates in the room. If the player targets Sigmund with a magic attack before Zanik, he switches prayers to protect magic, then again to protect range from Zanik. This then causes a bug where the player splashes constantly on Sigmund, but he will be vulnerable to ranged attacks, despite having [[Protect from Missiles]] active. {{Bug|When attacking Sigmund with the combat style he is praying against, it possible to deal 1 hitpoint of damage to him rather than 0.}} ==Another Slice of H.A.M.== In this quest, Sigmund and his men ambush [[goblin]]s at the [[Goblin Village]]. After a brief struggle, he captures [[Zanik]] and ties her to the new rail line linking [[Keldagrim]] and [[Dorgesh-Kaan]] in the hopes of starting war between the two cities. However, his plans are foiled by an adventurer who defeats him and manages to get Zanik off the track just before the train arrives. ===Combat Strategy=== This time, Sigmund is slightly harder to defeat. [[Zanik]] will not be able to help you, and his combat level has increased from level 50 to level 64 since the last encounter. He will activate protection prayers depending on which combat style the player attacks with. Use the [[Ancient mace|Ancient Mace]]'s [[Special attacks|Special Attack]] to drain his prayer in order to damage him. You can switch to a different weapon after his prayer is drained. He is immune to the effects of [[ring of recoil]]. ==Pickpocketing== {{Thieving info |name = Sigmund |level = 13 |xp = 0 |type = Pickpocket |tool = None }} {{DropsTableHead}} {{DropsLineSkill|name=Key (The Lost Tribe)|quantity=1|rarity=Always|raritynotes=Only during [[The Lost Tribe]].|skill=Thieving|gemw=No}} {{DropsTableBottom}} ==Dialogue== {{Hastranscript|npc}} ==Gallery== Sigmund eavesdropping.png|After being exposed, Sigmund eavesdrops on the peace treaty's signing. Sigmund plotting.png|Sigmund and Johanhus plotting the flooding of Dorgesh-Kaan. Sigmund teleports.png|Sigmund's ring of life teleports him to safety. Sigmund fighting.png|Sigmund duelling Zanik, protected by prayer. Another Slice Of H.A.M - Sigmund appears.png|Sigmund holding Zanik hostage after blinding her. Another Slice Of H.A.M - Zanik tied up.png|Waiting for the train to arrive... {{External|rs}} {{Infobox NPC |version1 = Normal |version2 = Imprisoned |version3 = Recovered |version4 = Disguised |name = Silif |image1 = [[File:Silif.png|110px]] |image2 = [[File:Silif (imprisoned).png|200px]] |image3 = [[File:Silif (recovered).png|110px]] |image4 = [[File:Silif (disguised).png|110px]] |release = [[10 July]] [[2024]] |update = While Guthix Sleeps |members = Yes |race = [[Human]] |quest = [[While Guthix Sleeps]] |location = [[Black Knight Catacombs]] |gender = Male |options = Talk-to |examine1 = A mysterious, sharply-dressed man. |examine2 = It looks like he wasn't quite stealthy enough. |examine3 = A mysterious, sharply-dressed man. |examine4 = The armour adds to his stealthiness. |map = {{Map|name=Silif|x=4135|y=4790|mapID=-1|plane=1|mtype=pin}} |id1 = 13519 |id2 = 13524 |id3 = 13520 |id4 = 13521 |leagueRegion = Asgarnia }} {{Synced switch |version1 = [[File:Silif chathead.png|left]] |version2 = [[File:Silif (imprisoned) chathead.png|left]] |version3 = [[File:Silif (imprisoned) chathead.png|left]] |version4 = [[File:Silif (disguised) chathead.png|left]] }} '''Silif''' is a [[Temple Knight]] operative working under [[Akrisae Kolluym]] as part of the alliance between the Temple Knights, the [[Guardians of Armadyl]], and the [[Guthix]]ian [[Crux Eqal]], who joined forces to oppose [[Lucien]]. He is known for having a good memory, and refers to the player's exploits as legendary.
During [[While Guthix Sleeps]], he is rescued from the [[Black Knight Catacombs]] after he was sent to investigate a reported sighting of the [[Dark Squall]], and returns to [[White Knights' Castle]] with details of the location of [[Lucien's camp]].
After completing the quest, the player can reobtain the [[Dark Squall robes]] from him in the White Knights' Castle if they have lost them.
==Dialogue== {{hastranscript|speaksin}}
==Trivia== * Silif is able to run while following the player in While Guthix Sleeps.
{{While Guthix Sleeps}} [[Category:Saradominists]]

revision.text:
{{Infobox Location |name = Silk Chasm |image = [[File:Silk Chasm.png|300px]] |release = [[25 January]] [[2023]] |update = Wilderness Boss Rework |members = Yes |location = [[Wilderness]] |race = [[Venenatis]] |wilderness = 35 |music = [[A Dangerous Game]] |map = [[File:Escape Caves map.png]] |type = dungeon |leagueRegion = Wilderness }} The '''Silk Chasm''' is the lair of [[Venenatis]]. It is a [[multi-combat]] [[dungeon]] located in the [[Wilderness]], just south-east of [[Callisto's Den]]. Entering the boss lair requires completion of the [[Wilderness Diary#Medium|medium Wilderness diary]] '''OR''' a Venenatis boss Slayer task, '''and''' a fee of 50,000 coins; this fee does not need to be brought along in the inventory, and can be deducted from the bank. This fee is shared across [[Callisto's Den]], [[Hunter's End]], the [[Skeletal Tomb]], [[Vet'ion's Rest]], the Silk Chasm, the [[Web Chasm]] and the [[Escape Caves]]. The fee does not need to be paid again, unless the player dies to another player without having left the Wilderness since their most recent visit to a boss lair or the Escape Caves. If this happens, the fee is dropped as loot for the killer, and needs to be paid again to re-enter the boss lairs. Players can decrease the fee by killing the six bosses; each kill in which the player deals the most damage to it reduces the fee by 10,000 coins.
[[File:Wilderness bosses map.png|thumb|left|300px|The entrances to the boss lairs and the Escape Caves.]] Like the [[Callisto's Den]] and [[Vet'ion's Rest]], players exiting the Silk Chasm will always arrive at one of three points within the [[Escape Caves]] at random. Note that any player who exits within 10 seconds of the previous player will arrive at the same point, meaning [[player killers]] can pursue their targets through the boss lair.
Upon any player entering the lair, all players inside will be unable to [[teleport]] for 3 [[ticks]]. This delay no longer occurs after completion of the [[Wilderness Diary#Hard|hard Wilderness diary]].
In order to peek inside the lair, the player must have at least 20 kills registered in their name.
==Gallery== <gallery mode="nolines" heights="180" style="text-align:left" widths="300"> Silk Chasm concept art.jpg|Concept art of the Silk Chasm, by [[Mod Jerv]]. </gallery>
==Changes== {{Subject changes header}} {{Subject changes |date = 14 February 2024 |update = Barbarian Training, Forestry Changes & More |change = The fee of 50,000 coins paid for accessing the lair is now only lost on death if the player pays the fee and dies before leaving the Wilderness. }} {{Subject changes |date = 20 September 2023 |update = Poll 80 & Shooting Stars Changes |change = * Players are now unable to teleport out of the [[Wilderness boss]] caves for 3 [[ticks]] after they enter. ** This delay can be avoided if players have completed the [[Wilderness Diary#Hard|hard Wilderness diary]]. * The 1-tick animation delay for players entering the dungeon has now been removed. }} {{Subject changes |date = 22 February 2023 |update = 10th Birthday Event |change = Players are now be able to engage in combat one tick sooner when entering the Silk Chasm. }} {{Subject changes footer}}
{{Dungeons}} {{Wilderness}}

{{Infobox Item |defver = 2 |version1 = 1 use |version2 = 2 uses |bucketname1 = (1) |bucketname2 = (2) |name1 = Silk dressing (1) |name2 = Silk dressing (2) |image1 = [[File:Silk dressing (1).png]] |image2 = [[File:Silk dressing (2).png]] |release = [[24 August]] [[2022]] |update = Tombs of Amascut |members = Yes |quest = No |tradeable = Yes |equipable = No |stackable = No |noteable = Yes |options = Apply, Drop |examine = Restores a large amount of health over time. |value = 30 |weight = 0.453 |id1 = 27325 |id2 = 27323 }} {{Synced switch |version1 = [[File:Silk dressing (1) detail.png|left|150px]] |version2 = [[File:Silk dressing (2) detail.png|left|150px]] }} '''Silk dressing''' is an item that can be obtained from the [[Supplies (Tombs of Amascut)|supplies bag]] within the [[Tombs of Amascut]].
Applying it will heal players by 5 hitpoints every 5 ticks (3 seconds) 20 times, for a total healing amount of 100 hitpoints over 100 ticks (60 seconds), and can boost the player's hitpoints up to 5 above their maximum.
As silk dressing is considered as a food item, it cannot be obtained if the "On a Diet" invocation is enabled.
{{Tombs of Amascut}}
